definition_zh: 立法者；议员；（州、准州或殖民地的）立法机关成员
definition_en: a person who takes part in making laws, especially a member of a legislature
core_image: 一个人站在长桌前，手里举着一页写满条文的纸，把它递向表决的灯
scene: 长桌前一个人举起一页条文，向身后的同僚示意可以表决了。 The legislator spent the morning explaining the bill to constituents.
sceneCN: 句中这个词指参与制定法律的个人，尤指立法机关成员（第 1 个义项：在立法机关中参与立法的成员）；句意为这位议员花了一上午向选民解释该法案。图中可辨识物件：长桌、条文纸页、表决灯、选区地图、记事本。

pos.zh: 立法者；议员（可数）
（美式）州、准州或殖民地立法机关成员

senses.title: A member of a legislature
senses.definition: a person who sits in a lawmaking body and votes on statutes
senses.definitionCN: 在立法机关中任职并对法规投票的人
senses.example: The legislator spent the morning explaining the bill to constituents.
senses.exampleCN: 这位议员花了一上午向选民解释该法案。
senses.why: The word is Latin legis lator, 'one who brings a law', so its first sense is simply the person who carries a bill through a chamber.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是拉丁 legis lator「把法律带来的人」，因此第一义就是那个把草案在议院里推过去的人。

senses.title: One who drafts or proposes a law
senses.definition: a person who frames the text of a proposed law rather than merely voting on it
senses.definitionCN: 拟定法律草案文本、而不只是投票的人
senses.example: As a legislator she drafted the clause on water rights.
senses.exampleCN: 作为立法者，她起草了关于水权的条款。
senses.why: The Latin phrase stresses proposing rather than sitting, so the word keeps a drafting sense alongside the parliamentary one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁短语强调的是「提出」而非「坐席」，因此这个词在议会义之外还保留起草义。

senses.title: A state or provincial lawmaker
senses.definition: in American usage, a member of a state, territorial or colonial legislature
senses.definitionCN: 在美式用法中，指州、准州或殖民地立法机关的成员
senses.example: Every state legislator faces re-election within two years.
senses.exampleCN: 每位州议员都要在两年内面对改选。
senses.why: American usage narrowed the word to the subnational chamber, where most lawmaking on local matters happens.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法把这个词收窄到地方议院，因为关于本地事务的立法多在那里发生。

senses.title: An ancient lawgiver
senses.definition: a historical figure credited with giving a people its code of law
senses.definitionCN: 被认为为一个民族立下法典的历史人物
senses.example: Solon is remembered as a legislator of Athens.
senses.exampleCN: 梭伦被铭记为雅典的立法者。
senses.why: The word is older than parliaments, so it naturally names the single founder of a code.
senses.whyCN: 这个词比议会更老，因此它自然可以指一个法典的单一创立者。

senses.title: A rule-setter inside an organisation
senses.titleCN: 组织内部的规则制定者
senses.definition: a person who writes the binding rules of a club, union or company
senses.definitionCN: 为社团、工会或公司编写有约束力规则的人
senses.example: The union's constitution makes each delegate a legislator for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 工会章程使每位代表在两年内成为规则制定者。
senses.why: Writing rules that bind others is the core function, so the title transfers to any body with rule-making power.
senses.whyCN: 写出约束他人的规则是核心职能，因此这个称号可转移到任何拥有立规权的团体。

senses.title: An arbiter of taste or fashion
senses.definition: a figurative use for someone whose choices set the standard others copy
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指其选择为他人树立标准的人
senses.example: The designer was called a legislator of style.
senses.exampleCN: 这位设计师被称为风格的立法者。
senses.why: A lawgiver fixes what is allowed; a taste-maker fixes what is admired, and the metaphor borrows that authority.
senses.whyCN: 立法者定下什么被允许；品味制定者定下什么被赞赏，这个比喻借用了那种权威。

senses.title: One who codifies a profession's rules
senses.definition: a person who writes a professional code of conduct or standards
senses.definitionCN: 编写行业行为准则或标准的人
senses.example: The physicians elected a legislator for their ethics code.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们推举一人为他们编写伦理准则。
senses.why: Professional codes are statutes in miniature, so their authors take a name from public law.
senses.whyCN: 行业准则像是缩小的法规，因此其作者借用了公法里的名称。

senses.title: A representative speaking for a district
senses.definition: a lawmaker regarded as the voice of the people who elected him or her
senses.definitionCN: 被视为其选民代言人的立法者
senses.example: Voters expect their legislator to answer letters.
senses.exampleCN: 选民期望自己的议员回复来信。
senses.why: Election turns a lawmaker into a delegate, so the word also carries the duty of speaking for others.
senses.whyCN: 选举把立法者变成代表，因此这个词也带着替他人发声的职责。

intro.en: Legislator is English from about 1600, taken from Latin legis lator 'proposer of a law'. Lex means 'law' and lator means 'bearer', the latter built on latus, the carried form of ferre 'to carry'.
intro.cn: legislator 约在 1600 年进入英语，取自拉丁 legis lator「法律的提出者」。lex 意为「法律」，lator 意为「搬运者」，后者由 ferre「搬运」的被动态 latus 构成。

items.en: Lex, genitive legis, meant 'law, statute'. Its deeper origin is unknown, and the link sometimes proposed to legere 'to read, gather' is a hypothesis, not a proof.
items.cn: lex（属格 legis）意为「法律、法令」。其更深来源不明，有时被提出的与 legere「读、收集」的联系只是假说，不是证明。

items.en: Ferre 'to carry' had the participle latus 'borne', which served as its past participle and also lies behind translate and relate.
items.cn: ferre「搬运」的分词 latus「被搬运的」，被当作它的过去分词使用，也是 translate 与 relate 的来源。

items.en: The Latin phrase named the person who brought a proposed law before the assembly; lator is the agent noun of the carrying verb.
items.cn: 这个拉丁短语命名把法律草案带到大会前的人；lator 是「搬运」动词的施事名词。

items.en: English legislator appears about 1600 with the general sense of lawgiver; the feminine legislatrix is recorded from the 1670s.
items.cn: 英语 legislator 约在 1600 年出现，泛指立法者；阴性形式 legislatrix 自十七世纪七十年代见于记录。

items.en: In the United States the noun settled on a member of a state, territorial or colonial legislature, a sense still dominant there.
items.cn: 在美国，这个名词固定指州、准州或殖民地立法机关的成员，这一义项至今在美式用法中占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain for the pre-Latin origin of lex; the date 1600 is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定之处是 lex 在拉丁语之前的来源；1600 年是约数。

note.en: Group one holds the law-family nouns and the look-alike reading-family words; group two holds people who also make or speak for laws.
note.cn: 第一组是法律词族的名词，以及形似的「读」词族词；第二组是同样立法或代言的其他人。

entries.definition: The institution, not one member; the -ure ending marks an office or body.
entries.definitionCN: 指机构，不是单个成员；-ure 词尾标记职务或机构。

entries.definition: The laws produced or the act of producing them; it names a result, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指产出的法规或立法行为；命名结果，不指人。

entries.definition: Relating to lawmaking; it describes a power or session rather than a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指与立法有关的；描述权力或会期，而非人。

entries.definition: Readable, from legere 'to read'; the shared letters do not make it a relative of lex.
entries.definitionCN: 指可读的，出自 legere「读」；相同的字母并不使它成为 lex 的同族。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a person who makes laws; legislator is its formal equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 指制定法律者的日常说法；legislator 是其正式对应词。

entries.definition: A person who gives a whole code to a people, like Solon; it suits the historical sense better than the parliamentary one.
entries.definitionCN: 指像梭伦那样把一个完整法典交给一个民族的人；更贴合历史义而非议会义。

entries.definition: An elected person who acts for a constituency; the emphasis is on speaking for others, not on drafting text.
entries.definitionCN: 指为选区行事的民选者；强调替他人发声，而非撰写条文。

entries.definition: A member skilled in parliamentary rules; the word stresses procedural knowledge rather than lawmaking itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指精通议会规则的人；这个词强调程序知识，而非立法本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin compound, the real family and the real institutional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁复合词、真实词族与真实的机构搭配。

normal.en: legis 'of law' plus lator 'bearer': the person who carries a bill.
normal.cn: legis「法律的」加 lator「搬运者」：把草案搬过去的那个人。

normal.en: The family runs legislate, legislation, legislative, legislature and legislator.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 legislate、legislation、legislative、legislature 与 legislator。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the role: state legislator, elected legislator, the legislator's duty.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角色：州议员、当选议员、议员的职责。

normal.en: The -or ending marks the doer; the -ure ending marks the body.
normal.cn: 词尾 -or 标记施事者，-ure 标记机构。

normal.en: Latin lex is the law root; legere, the reading root, is a different family.
normal.cn: 拉丁 lex 是法律词根；legere 是「读」的词根，属另一词族。

abstract.en: Picture one hand raising a page so that a whole room can see it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起一页纸，让整间屋子都看见。

abstract.en: Picture a single brick laid into a wall that will outlast the mason.
abstract.cn: 想象一块砖砌进一堵比砌砖人活得更久的墙。

abstract.en: Picture a pen that signs for people who never meet the writer.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔替从未见过作者的人签名。

examples.en: The legislator introduced a bill on rural clinics.
examples.cn: 这位议员提出了一项关于乡村诊所的法案。

examples.en: A territorial legislator could not vote on national tariffs.
examples.cn: 准州议员无权对国家关税投票。

examples.en: Reformers praised her as a legislator who read every amendment.
examples.cn: 改革者称赞她是一位逐条读修正案的立法者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 legis-累-斯雷-特」——一位特别「累」的人，把一条条「斯雷」的法令搬进议场 → 立法者

root: 拉丁 legis lator「法律的提出者」= lex（属格 legis）「法律」+ lator「搬运者」（ferre「搬运」的被动态 latus）；lex 更深来源不明。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person: a member voting in a chamber, a drafter of text, a state member, an ancient founder, a small-scale rule-setter, an arbiter of taste, a writer of professional codes and a voice for a district.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个人展开：在议院投票的成员、条文的起草者、州议员、古代立法者、小范围规则制定者、品味裁定者、行业准则编写者、选区代言人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand raising a page of clauses before a room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在满屋人面前举起一页条文。

branches.en: SEAT AND VOICE: sitting in the chamber and speaking for a district are two halves of one mandate.
branches.cn: 席位与声音：坐在议院里与替选区发声，是同一项授权的两半。

branches.en: WRITING RULES: drafting a statute and codifying a profession both mean putting binding words on paper.
branches.cn: 写下规则：起草法规与编定行业准则，都是把有约束力的话写到纸上。

branches.en: THE LOWER CHAMBER: American usage keeps the word close to local lawmaking.
branches.cn: 下级议院：美式用法让这个词贴近地方立法。

branches.en: THE FOUNDER: before parliaments, the word named the single giver of a code.
branches.cn: 创立者：在议会之前，这个词指单独给出法典的人。

branches.en: BORROWED AUTHORITY: a club or a fashion world can borrow the lawgiver's authority for its own rules.
branches.cn: 借来的权威：社团或时尚界都能借用立法者的权威来立自己的规矩。

intro.en: The word is a Latin compound wrapped in an English agent ending, so each piece has its own English offspring.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个外裹英语施事词尾的拉丁复合词，每一部分都有自己的英语后代。

latinIntro.en: Lex gives legal and legislation; the carrying verb gives lator, translate and relate; -or marks the person.
latinIntro.cn: lex 提供 legal 与 legislation；搬运动词提供 lator、translate 与 relate；-or 标记人。

items.example: The root names what the person carries.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名人所搬运之物。

items.example: The noun names the carrier of the bill.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名草案的搬运者。

items.example: The chamber can legislate on health.
The legislation passed by one vote.
items.exampleCN: 这项法规以一票之差通过。

items.example: The legislative session opens in January.
The ending marks a person, not a body.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记人，不标记机构。

items.example: The adjective legislatorial follows the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 legislatorial 遵循同样的模式。

latinEntries.structure: latus, lata, latum (past participle of ferre)

definition_zh: 拱廊；有拱廊的街道；（旧）拱廊商铺街；电子游戏厅
definition_en: a passage with a roof lined by arches along one or both sides; also a hall of coin-operated games
core_image: 一排石拱肩并肩：柱影连成长长的清凉通道
scene: 老城午后，游客走进连拱的骑楼躲避烈日。 Shoppers strolled along the shaded arcade of the old city.
sceneCN: 这里 arcade 是「拱廊」（第 1 个义项：由连续拱券构成的通道）；句意为：顾客们在老城荫凉的拱廊里漫步。

pos.zh: 拱廊；拱廊街；游戏厅

derivatives.zh: 过去分词转形容词，义为「带有连拱的」

senses.title: A passage lined with arches
senses.definition: a covered walkway formed by a row of arches and columns
senses.definitionCN: 由一列拱券与柱子构成的带顶步道
senses.example: Sunlight flickered through the stone arcade.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光在石拱廊间忽明忽暗。
senses.why: The root arcus means bow or arch; repeated arches build a passage.
senses.whyCN: 词根 arcus 意为弓、拱；连续的拱便构成通道。

senses.title: A row of shops under arches
senses.definition: a street of shops sheltered by an arched roof
senses.definitionCN: 由拱顶遮蔽的一街店铺
senses.example: The nineteenth-century arcade houses forty boutiques.
senses.exampleCN: 这座十九世纪的拱廊街开有四十家精品店。
senses.why: The covered walk became a market street.
senses.whyCN: 带顶步道演变为市集街。

senses.title: A roofed shopping gallery
senses.definition: a modern glass-roofed passage of stores, as in European arcades
senses.definitionCN: 现代玻璃顶商业通道，如欧洲的拱廊街
senses.example: Rain could not spoil their day in the glass arcade.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨也毁不掉他们在玻璃拱廊的一天。
senses.why: Architecture keeps the arch and adds glass and steel.
senses.whyCN: 建筑保留拱券，添上玻璃与钢。

senses.title: A decorative range of arches
senses.definition: a series of arches on a building face with no passage behind
senses.definitionCN: 建筑立面上并无通道的一列拱券
senses.example: Blind arcades decorate the cathedral wall.
senses.exampleCN: 假拱装饰着大教堂的墙面。
senses.why: The arch sequence can be pure ornament.
senses.whyCN: 拱列可以纯粹作为装饰。

senses.title: A hall of coin games
senses.definition: a place with coin-operated video and amusement machines
senses.definitionCN: 摆放投币式电子游戏机与游艺机的场所
senses.example: Teenagers crowded the arcade after school.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后少年们挤满了游戏厅。
senses.why: Amusement piers called their game halls arcades, and the name stuck.
senses.whyCN: 游乐场把游戏厅叫作 arcade，名字就此固定。

senses.title: A public amenity passage
senses.definition: a sheltered shortcut through a city block
senses.definitionCN: 穿过街区带顶棚的近道
senses.example: Cut through the arcade to reach the station.
senses.exampleCN: 穿过拱廊就能到车站。
senses.why: Covered passages serve as shortcuts in bad weather.
senses.whyCN: 带顶通道在坏天气里充当捷径。

senses.title: Architectural rhythm of arches
senses.definition: the pattern of arches as a defining feature of a style
senses.definitionCN: 作为风格特征的拱券序列
senses.example: Romanesque arcades mark the abbey's nave.
senses.exampleCN: 罗马式连拱是大教堂中殿的标志。
senses.why: Repeated arches create visual music.
senses.whyCN: 重复的拱券构成视觉音乐。

senses.title: A heritage covered market
senses.definition: a preserved historic arcade valued as architecture
senses.definitionCN: 作为建筑遗产被保存的历史拱廊
senses.example: The gallery arcade was restored to its 1890s look.
senses.exampleCN: 这座拱廊街被修复回十九世纪九十年代的原貌。
senses.why: Old arcades became treasures worth keeping.
senses.whyCN: 老拱廊成了值得保存的珍宝。

intro.en: Arcade comes from French arcage and Italian arcata, an arch, from Latin arcus, bow or arch.
intro.cn: arcade 经法语 arcage 与意大利语 arcata（拱）而来，词根是拉丁语 arcus（弓、拱）。

items.en: The reconstructed root *arku- meant to bend or curve, as a drawn bow.
items.cn: 重构词根 *arku- 意为弯曲，如张开的弓。

items.en: Arcus meant a bow or an arch built of stone.
items.cn: arcus 意为弓或石砌拱券。

items.en: Arcata and arcage named a single arch, then a row of arches.
items.cn: arcata 与 arcage 先指单个拱，继而指一列拱。

items.en: English adopted arcade in the seventeenth century for architectural arch-ranges.
items.cn: 英语十七世纪借入 arcade，指建筑上的连拱。

items.en: The word widened to covered shopping streets and then to coin-game halls.
items.cn: 词义扩展到带顶商业街，再转到投币游戏厅。

note.en: Arcade belongs to the arcus family of arch and curve words.
note.cn: arcade 属于 arcus「弓、拱」词族。

entries.definition: a curved structure spanning an opening
entries.definitionCN: 拱；拱门

entries.definition: one who shoots with a bow
entries.definitionCN: 弓箭手

entries.definition: a curved line or path
entries.definitionCN: 弧线；弧

entries.definition: a row of columns, roofed or not
entries.definitionCN: 柱廊

entries.definition: a covered passage or elevated walkway
entries.definitionCN: 廊道；画廊

entries.definition: a covered walk around a monastery court
entries.definitionCN: 修道院回廊

normalIntro.en: The arc root draws the whole word for you.
normalIntro.cn: arc 词根替你画出了整个词。

normal.en: arcade = arc (arch) + -ade (a row or action): a row of arches.
normal.cn: arcade = arc（拱）+ -ade（一列/动作）：一列拱。

normal.en: Same root as arch, arc, archer.
normal.cn: 与 arch、arc、archer 同根。

normal.en: Two modern meanings: shopping arcade and video arcade.
normal.cn: 两大现代义：购物拱廊街与电子游戏厅。

normal.en: Suffix parallel: arcade, cavalcade, blockade — all -ade nouns.
normal.cn: 后缀平行：arcade、cavalcade、blockade 都是 -ade 名词。

normal.en: Image anchor: columns repeating like the beat of a drum.
normal.cn: 意象锚点：柱子如鼓点般重复。

abstract.en: A stone caterpillar of arches walking down a street.
abstract.cn: 一条石头毛毛虫拱着背沿街爬行。

abstract.en: A row of rainbows holding up a roof.
abstract.cn: 一排彩虹托起屋顶。

abstract.en: Arcade sounds like 'are-cade': arches parade in a row.
abstract.cn: arcade 听着像 are-cade：拱门列队行进。

examples.en: The arcade connects the two squares downtown.
examples.cn: 这条拱廊连接着市中心的两个广场。

examples.en: A coin arcade occupied the basement for decades.
examples.cn: 那间游戏厅在地下室开了几十年。

examples.en: Artisans' stalls lined the medieval arcade.
examples.cn: 中世纪拱廊下排满手工艺人的摊位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿凯」——阿凯家住在拱廊街口，谐音仅助记，词源仍是 arc（拱）。

root: 拉丁词根 arc-/arch-（弓、拱，arcus）：arcade 经意大利语 arcata、法语 arcage 而来，本义「一列拱券」，引申为拱廊街，再引申为游戏厅；同根词有 arch、arc、archer。

sensesIntro.en: From a row of arches, arcade grows into shop-lined passages, glass galleries, decorative arch-ranges, game halls, shortcuts, architectural rhythm, and preserved heritage arcades.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「一列拱券」出发，arcade 生长为拱廊商铺街、玻璃商业廊、装饰假拱、游戏厅、便道捷径、拱券韵律与受保护的遗产拱廊。

definition_zh: 盐度；含盐量；咸度
definition_en: the amount of dissolved salt contained in water or soil, usually measured in parts per thousand
core_image: 一支比重计插进水样，刻度停在一个数上，数值越高，水就越咸
scene: 海洋调查船上，技术员把探头放进一桶刚打上来的水说， The salinity here is high enough to float an egg.
sceneCN: 这里 salinity 指「水中溶解盐的含量」（第 1 个义项：以千分比表示的含盐量）；句意为：这里的盐度高到能让鸡蛋浮起来。

pos.zh: 盐度；含盐量；（土壤）盐渍化程度

senses.title: The amount of salt dissolved in water
senses.definition: the quantity of dissolved salts in water, considered as a measurable property of the water
senses.definitionCN: 水中溶解盐的数量，被视为水的一项可测属性
senses.example: The salinity here is high enough to float an egg.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的盐度高到能让鸡蛋浮起来。
senses.why: Latin sal 'salt' plus the adjective suffix -inus and the noun suffix -ity produce a word that names a quality, so salinity is salt-ness measured rather than salt itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 sal「盐」加形容词后缀 -inus 与名词后缀 -ity，造出一个指性质的名词，因此 salinity 是可被测量的「咸的程度」，而不是盐本身。

senses.title: The oceanographic measurement
senses.titleCN: 海洋学中的盐度计量值
senses.definition: the standard measure of sea water's salt content, reported in parts per thousand or on the practical salinity scale
senses.definitionCN: 海水含盐量的标准量值，以千分比或实用盐度标度表示
senses.example: Surface salinity falls sharply where the river empties into the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 河水注入海湾处，表层盐度急剧下降。
senses.why: a property that varies from place to place needs a scale, and oceanography fixed one so that a number on a chart means the same thing on every ship.
senses.whyCN: 一项随地点变化的属性需要一个标度，海洋学因此固定了一套，使海图上的一个数字在每条船上都表示同一件事。

senses.title: Salt accumulated in soil
senses.definition: the concentration of salts left in soil, often after irrigation water evaporates
senses.definitionCN: 留在土壤中的盐分浓度，常由灌溉水蒸发后形成
senses.example: Years of flood irrigation raised the salinity of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 多年大水漫灌提高了这块田的盐度。
senses.why: water brought to a dry field carries a little salt, and when the water leaves by evaporation the salt stays; repeat that and the soil itself becomes the container.
senses.whyCN: 引到旱地的水带着少量盐，水蒸发离开后盐却留下；如此反复，土壤本身就成了盛盐的容器。

senses.title: The gradient in an estuary
senses.definition: the gradual change from fresh river water to salt sea water across an estuary
senses.definitionCN: 河口处从淡水到海水逐渐变化的盐度过渡
senses.example: Oysters cluster where the salinity stays between fresh and full sea.
senses.exampleCN: 牡蛎聚集在盐度介于淡水与全海水之间的地带。
senses.why: two waters meet without mixing at once, so salinity becomes a map of distance from the river mouth rather than a single number.
senses.whyCN: 两种水相遇却不会立刻混匀，因此盐度成了一张标示离河口远近的地图，而不是一个孤立的数字。

senses.title: The limit an organism can bear
senses.titleCN: 生物所能承受的盐度上限
senses.definition: the range of salt concentration within which a plant or animal can survive
senses.definitionCN: 某种动植物能够存活的含盐浓度范围
senses.example: Few crops have enough salinity tolerance for that coastal soil.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有作物对那片沿海土壤具有足够的耐盐性。
senses.why: for a living thing the number stops being chemistry and becomes a threshold: above it, water is pulled out of the cells and the organism fails.
senses.whyCN: 对生物而言，这个数字不再是化学，而是阈值：超过它，水被从细胞中抽走，生物便无法存活。

senses.title: The difference used to make power
senses.definition: the difference in salt concentration between two waters, exploited to drive turbines or cells
senses.definitionCN: 两种水之间含盐浓度的差异，被用来驱动涡轮或电池
senses.example: The pilot plant runs on the salinity difference between river and sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这座试验电厂靠河水与海水的盐度差运转。
senses.why: mixing salt and fresh water releases energy that was stored in the separation, so the measurement itself becomes a fuel gauge.
senses.whyCN: 咸淡水混合会释放储存在分离状态中的能量，因此这个量值本身就成了燃料表。

senses.title: Salt strength in food and brine
senses.definition: the salt concentration of a brine, sauce or preserved food, judged by taste or by recipe
senses.definitionCN: 卤水、酱汁或腌制品中的盐浓度，按口味或配方判断
senses.example: The cheesemaker checks the brine's salinity before soaking the curds.
senses.exampleCN: 奶酪师在浸泡凝乳前先检查卤水的咸度。
senses.why: the kitchen uses the same idea at a smaller scale: brine is sea water made on purpose, and its salinity decides how much water leaves the food.
senses.whyCN: 厨房以更小的尺度使用同一观念：卤水是人工配制的海水，其盐度决定有多少水从食物中被抽出。

senses.title: A water-quality limit for irrigation
senses.titleCN: 灌溉水质中的盐度限值
senses.definition: the salt level of irrigation water above which crops or pipes are harmed
senses.definitionCN: 灌溉水含盐量超过即会损害作物或管道的水平
senses.example: The agency sets a salinity limit for water released into farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构为排入农田的水设定了盐度限值。
senses.why: once water is managed, the property becomes a rule on paper: a threshold that decides whether a river may be used on a field.
senses.whyCN: 一旦水被管理，这项属性就变成纸面上的规则：一个决定河水能否用于农田的阈值。

senses.title: A clue to past climate
senses.definition: an ancient salt level read from sediments or ice, used to reconstruct past ocean and climate conditions
senses.definitionCN: 从沉积物或冰芯中读出的古代含盐量，用来重建过去的海洋与气候状况
senses.example: The core's salinity record shows a sudden shift in rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯的盐度记录显示降雨曾突然改变。
senses.why: salt leaves a chemical trace in mud and ice, so a value measured today can stand for a sea that disappeared long ago.
senses.whyCN: 盐在泥沙与冰中留下化学痕迹，因此今天测得的数值可以代表一片早已消失的海。

intro.en: Salinity is a Latin-based noun: sal 'salt' produced the adjective salinus 'of salt', and English added -ity to name the quality. The modern scientific sense developed in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: salinity 是拉丁系名词：sal「盐」构成形容词 salinus「盐的」，英语再加 -ity 命名这一性质；现代科学义到 19 世纪才发展起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sal, salis is the Latin noun for salt; it is the base of a large family including salinus, salarium and the verb salire 'to salt'.
items.cn: Sal, salis 是拉丁语中指盐的名词；它是 salinus、salarium 以及动词 salire「加盐」等一大批词的基干。

items.en: Salinus 'of salt, salty' adds -inus to sal; English saline comes directly from this adjective.
items.cn: salinus「盐的、咸的」在 sal 后加 -inus；英语 saline 直接来自这个形容词。

items.en: The Latin noun suffix -itas (English -ity) turns an adjective into a name for a quality, which is the pattern behind salinity, clarity and humidity.
items.cn: 拉丁名词后缀 -itas（英语作 -ity）把形容词变成指性质的名词，salinity、clarity、humidity 都循这一模式。

items.en: English salinity is recorded from the nineteenth century, when chemistry and oceanography needed a technical noun distinct from the everyday word saltiness.
items.cn: 英语 salinity 的书证见于 19 世纪，当时化学与海洋学需要一个区别于日常词 saltiness 的技术名词。

items.en: In the twentieth century salinity was tied to electrical conductivity and later to a practical scale, so that a measured number could be compared across oceans and decades.
items.cn: 20 世纪，盐度与电导率挂钩，后来又绑定到一套实用标度，使测得的数值可以跨大洋、跨年代比较。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, not root): the earliest English citation is not precisely fixed, and the exact route through French salinité is generally accepted but not documented step by step; the Indo-European form *sal- behind Latin sal is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，不涉及词根）：英语最早书证没有确切年份；经法语 salinité 传入的路径属于「一般认为是」，但缺少逐步文献；拉丁 sal 背后的印欧形式 *sal- 是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like salinity but do not all share the salt root; group two holds measures and qualities of salt water.
note.cn: 第一组是与 salinity 形近、但并非都同出盐词根的词；第二组是海水含盐量的相关说法。

entries.definition: the adjective from Latin salinus, meaning containing salt; salinity is the noun built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 salinus 的形容词，意为含盐的；salinity 是由它构成的名词。

entries.definition: the process by which soil or water becomes salty; it names the change, while salinity names the amount.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤或水变咸的过程；它指变化，而 salinity 指数量。

entries.definition: from Latin sanus 'healthy': soundness of mind. It looks close to salinity but has no salt in it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 sanus「健康的」：神志健全。它与 salinity 形近，却与盐毫无关系。

entries.definition: salt-bearing, from sal plus -ferous 'carrying'; it describes rock or springs, not a measured amount.
entries.definitionCN: 含盐的，由 sal 加 -ferous「携带」构成；它描写岩石或泉，而不是一个测得的量。

entries.definition: the plain English word for how salty something tastes; salinity is its scientific counterpart for water and soil.
entries.definitionCN: 指尝起来有多咸的日常英语词；salinity 是它在水与土壤领域的技术对应词。

entries.definition: the quality of being slightly salty, as in an estuary; it covers only the middle of the salinity range.
entries.definitionCN: 指略带咸味的性质，如河口；它只覆盖盐度范围的中间段。

entries.definition: the mass of chloride in sea water, historically used to calculate salinity; it measures one ion, not all salts.
entries.definitionCN: 海水中氯的质量，历史上用来推算盐度；它测的是一种离子，而非全部盐类。

entries.definition: the mass of all dissolved material in water, of which salt is only a part; the term is broader than salinity.
entries.definitionCN: 水中全部溶解物质的质量，盐只是其中一部分；这个术语比 salinity 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin sal 'salt' plus -inus plus -ity: salt-ness turned into a measurable noun.
normal.cn: 拉丁 sal「盐」加 -inus 再加 -ity：把「咸」变成可测量的名词。

normal.en: The family runs saline, salinity, salinization, salinize, desalination, salimeter.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 saline、salinity、salinization、salinize、desalination、salimeter。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical sense: surface salinity, soil salinity, salinity gradient, salinity tolerance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：表层盐度、土壤盐度、盐度梯度、耐盐性。

normal.en: The everyday word is saltiness; salinity is what a laboratory reports.
normal.cn: 日常说法是 saltiness；salinity 是实验室报告里的用词。

normal.en: Oceanographers often report salinity in parts per thousand, written with the per-mille sign.
normal.cn: 海洋学家常以千分比报告盐度，写作千分号。

abstract.en: Picture a float that sits higher in the glass the saltier the water becomes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只浮子，水越咸，它在杯中就浮得越高。

abstract.en: Picture a field that turns white after the irrigation water dries.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田在灌溉水干后泛出白色。

abstract.en: Picture a river and a sea meeting but keeping their separate colours for a while.

examples.en: Irrigation without drainage slowly raises soil salinity.
examples.cn: 只灌不排会慢慢提高土壤盐度。

examples.en: The instrument logs salinity every ten metres of depth.
examples.cn: 仪器每下潜十米记录一次盐度。

root: 拉丁 sal「盐」→ salinus「盐的、咸的」+ 名词后缀 -itas/-ity → 英语 salinity；同根另有 saline、salarium（盐钱→薪水）、desalination。拉丁 sal 的印欧来源 *sal- 为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one number as it changes hands: a property of water, a scale on a chart, a crust in a field, a gradient in an estuary, a survival limit, a fuel, a brine recipe, a legal threshold, and a trace of ancient rain.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个数值换手：水的属性、海图上的标度、田里的盐壳、河口的梯度、生存的上限、燃料、卤水配方、法定阈值，以及古代降雨的痕迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hydrometer standing in a sample, its scale marking how salty the water is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支比重计立在水样中，刻度标出这水有多咸。

branches.en: WHAT IS COUNTED: the quality itself, then the scale that lets one ship's number be compared with another's.
branches.cn: 数的是什么：先是性质本身，然后是让一条船的数字能与另一条船比较的标度。

branches.en: ON LAND: evaporation leaves salt in the field, and managers turn the measure into a legal limit.
branches.cn: 在陆地上：蒸发把盐留在田里，管理者再把这一量值变成法定限值。

branches.en: ACROSS SPACE AND TIME: a gradient maps the estuary, and a sediment core maps ancient rainfall.
branches.cn: 跨空间与时间：梯度绘出河口，沉积岩芯绘出古代降雨。

branches.en: AT THE THRESHOLD: too much salt stops a crop, and the right amount preserves a cheese.
branches.cn: 在阈值上：盐太多作物就活不了，盐适量则能腌好奶酪。

branches.en: AS FUEL: the difference between salt and fresh water can be spent as electricity.
branches.cn: 当作燃料：咸水与淡水之间的差异可以当作电来花。

intro.en: Salinity is built from a Latin root and two suffixes, and the same pieces recur across chemistry and water science.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sal 衍生 salinus、salarium 以及类似 salinitas 的构词；-ity 后缀是拉丁 -itas 在英语中的对应形式。

sensesIntro.en: Whether it lifts a paperback at a desk or a Bible in a church, a bookrest only changes one angle: the one between eye and page.
sensesIntro.cn: 无论在书桌上抬起平装书，还是在教堂里托起圣经，阅书架改变的都是同一个角度：眼睛与书页之间的角度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden frame holding an open book at just the right slant
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木架把摊开的书托成恰到好处的斜角

branches.en: A desk frame tilted to five positions.
branches.cn: 能调五个档位的桌面书架。

branches.en: Two pieces of oak under a paperback.
branches.cn: 平装书下的两块橡木。

branches.en: A brass stand holding the parish Bible.
branches.cn: 托着本堂圣经的黄铜书台。

branches.en: Carved wood under a leather register.
branches.cn: 托着皮面登记簿的雕花木台。

branches.en: One angle, changed for the reader.
branches.cn: 为读者改变的一个角度。

intro.en: Bookrest is book plus rest, an old noun for a prop; the list below covers both halves and the vocabulary of reading furniture.
intro.cn: bookrest 是 book 加 rest，rest 是古老的「支撑物」名词；下面列出它的两半，以及「阅读家具」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere is to read, restare is to remain or stand back, and fulcire is to prop.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为读，restare 意为停留或立于其后，fulcire 意为支撑。

latinEntries.exampleCN: legere 产生 lectern 与 lecture。
restare 是 rest 的来源。

definition_zh: 冷锋；冷锋过境；冷锋云带；冷锋后的降温
definition_en: the leading edge of a cold air mass advancing into warmer air, marked by squalls and a sharp temperature drop
core_image: 一堵冷空气的陡坡把暖空气顶上去，锋后天空转晴，气温骤然下降
scene: 午后西边的云墙压来，气温在一个小时里掉了好几摄氏度。 The cold front brought squalls and a sharp drop in temperature.
sceneCN: 这里指「冷气团向暖气团推进的交界面及其过境」（第 1 个义项：冷空气前沿的锋面）；句意为冷锋带来狂风阵雨，并伴随气温骤降。图中可辨识物件：压来的云墙、被顶升的暖空气、转向的风向标、骤降的温度计。

pos.zh: 冷锋；冷锋过境；冷锋云带

senses.title: The advancing edge of cold air
senses.definition: the boundary along which a colder air mass pushes under and lifts a warmer one
senses.definitionCN: 较冷气团从下方楔入并抬升较暖气团的交界面
senses.example: The cold front brought squalls and a sharp drop in temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 冷锋带来狂风阵雨，并伴随气温骤降。
senses.why: Cold air is denser, so it moves like a wedge under the warmer air rather than riding over it.
senses.whyCN: 冷空气密度更大，因此像楔子一样钻到暖空气下方，而非爬到它上面。

senses.title: The weather of its passage
senses.definition: the sequence of squalls, heavy showers, wind shift and falling temperature as the front passes
senses.definitionCN: 锋面经过时出现的飑、强阵雨、风向转变与降温序列
senses.example: During the cold front passage the wind veered and the rain turned torrential.
senses.exampleCN: 冷锋过境时风向顺转，雨势变得猛烈。
senses.why: The passage is an event with a beginning and an end, so the phrase names the whole sequence.
senses.whyCN: 过境是有始有终的事件，因此这个短语命名整个序列。

senses.title: A steep and fast-moving surface
senses.titleCN: 陡峭而移动较快的锋面
senses.definition: the relatively steep slope and rapid advance that distinguish a cold front from a warm front
senses.definitionCN: 使冷锋区别于暖锋的较陡坡度与较快推进速度
senses.example: Its steep slope squeezed the rain into a narrow band.
senses.exampleCN: 其陡峭的坡度把降雨压缩成一条窄带。
senses.why: Friction slows cold air near the ground, but the wedge still advances faster than a warm front.
senses.whyCN: 摩擦使近地面的冷空气减速，但整个楔体仍比暖锋推进得快。

senses.title: The narrow cloud band along it
senses.definition: the line of cumulus and cumulonimbus cloud that marks the front on satellite images
senses.definitionCN: 卫星图像上标示锋面的积云与积雨云线
senses.example: A cold-frontal cloud band stretched from the coast inland.
senses.exampleCN: 一条冷锋云带从海岸向内陆延伸。
senses.why: Forced ascent is concentrated in a narrow zone, so the cloud appears as a line rather than a sheet.
senses.whyCN: 被迫抬升集中在狭窄地带，因此云呈线状而非片状。

senses.title: Clear, dry air behind the front
senses.definition: the subsiding, cooler and often clearer air that follows the passage of a cold front
senses.definitionCN: 冷锋过境后下沉、较冷且常更晴朗的空气
senses.example: Behind the cold front the visibility improved within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 冷锋之后一小时之内能见度就改善了。
senses.why: Cold air sinking behind the front dries the lower atmosphere and clears the cloud.
senses.whyCN: 锋后下沉的冷空气使低层大气变干，云也随之消散。

senses.title: The leading edge of a cold outbreak
senses.definition: the front that marks the arrival of a large cold-air outbreak, often with gales and snow
senses.definitionCN: 标示大规模冷空气爆发到达的锋面，常伴大风与降雪
senses.example: The cold front preceded three days of hard frost.
senses.exampleCN: 冷锋之后是连续三天的严霜。
senses.why: A strong front is simply the visible edge of a much larger cold advance.
senses.whyCN: 强锋面不过是一次更大规模冷空气推进的可见边缘。

senses.title: The triangular symbol on a chart
senses.titleCN: 天气图上的三角形符号
senses.definition: the line of filled triangles drawn on a synoptic chart to show the direction of advance of cold air
senses.definitionCN: 天气图上用实心三角形标示冷空气推进方向的线
senses.example: On the chart, the cold front ran south-west with its triangles pointing east.
senses.exampleCN: 图上冷锋向西南延伸，三角形朝东指。
senses.why: The symbol encodes what the words say: the triangles point the way the cold air is going.
senses.whyCN: 符号把文字所说的内容编码：三角形指向冷空气推进的方向。

senses.title: An abrupt cooling in a relationship
senses.definition: a sudden, sharp change to a colder or more distant mood between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人与人、群体与群体之间骤然转向冷淡或疏远的变化
senses.example: The verdict acted as a cold front between the two ministries.
senses.exampleCN: 这一裁决成了两个部门之间的冷锋。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps only the sudden drop and the line of separation.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻只保留骤降与分隔之线两层意思。

intro.en: Cold front joins the native adjective cold, from Old English cald, with front, from Latin frons 'forehead, front'. Meteorology coined the phrase in the early twentieth century for the advancing edge of cold air.
intro.cn: cold front 由本族形容词 cold（古英语 cald）与 front（拉丁 frons「额头、正面」）组合。气象学在 20 世纪初用这个短语指冷空气推进的前沿。

items.en: Cald is the native word for low temperature, cognate with German kalt and Dutch koud.
items.cn: cald 是表示低温的本族词，与德语 kalt、荷兰语 koud 同源。

items.en: Front came through French from Latin frons, frontis, meaning the forehead and then any forward face or line.
items.cn: front 经法语来自拉丁 frons, frontis，指额头，进而指任何朝前的一面或线。

items.en: The Norwegian forecasters of the 1910s and 1920s separated cold fronts from warm fronts and drew them with triangles and semicircles.
items.cn: 20 世纪一十至二十年代的挪威预报员把冷锋与暖锋分开，并用三角形与半圆标绘。

items.en: The phrase only makes sense within air-mass theory: a front is the edge of a body of cold air.
items.cn: 这个短语只有放在气团理论中才成立：锋面是一团冷空气的边缘。

items.en: Twentieth-century aviation and warning services fixed the compound in routine forecasts.
items.cn: 20 世纪的航空与警报服务把这个复合词固定在日常预报中。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the first printed use of the exact phrase is dated differently in different sources; its formation and meaning are settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：该确切短语最早的书证在不同文献中年代不一；其构成与含义已经确定。

note.en: Group one holds the sibling front types and the base word; group two holds names for the cold air itself and its outbreak.
note.cn: 第一组是同类锋型与原词；第二组是冷空气本身及其爆发的名称。

entries.definition: The general boundary between air masses; it does not say which body is advancing.
entries.definitionCN: 气团间的一般交界；不说明哪一团在推进。

entries.definition: The leading edge of warm air riding over cold air, with gentle slope and steady rain.
entries.definitionCN: 暖空气爬到冷空气之上的前沿，坡度平缓、降雨持续。

entries.definition: The boundary left when a cold front catches a warm front and lifts it clear of the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 冷锋追上暖锋并把暖空气完全抬离地面后留下的交界。

entries.definition: A period of unusually low temperature over a region; it is the consequence, not the boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区一段异常低温时期；它是后果，而非交界。

entries.definition: A rapid spread of cold continental air over a warmer surface; the front is its leading edge.
entries.definitionCN: 冷大陆空气迅速铺展到较暖表面；冷锋是其前沿。

entries.definition: A strong cold north wind in the Gulf of Mexico region, usually following a cold front.
entries.definitionCN: 墨西哥湾地区强劲的冷北风，通常出现在冷锋之后。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real native cold, the real Latin front and the real Bergen symbols.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族「冷」、真实的拉丁「正面」与真实的卑尔根符号。

normal.en: Cold is native, front is Latin: the phrase is a hybrid, like the science that coined it.
normal.cn: cold 是本族词，front 是拉丁词：这个短语是混合体，正如造出它的学科。

normal.en: Cold air is denser, so it wedges under warm air.
normal.cn: 冷空气密度更大，因此楔入暖空气下方。

normal.en: Behind the front: clearing, drying and cooling.
normal.cn: 锋后：转晴、变干、降温。

normal.en: On a chart, triangles point the way the cold air moves.
normal.cn: 天气图上，三角形指向冷空气移动的方向。

normal.en: The passage is an event: squall, wind shift, temperature drop.
normal.cn: 过境是一个事件：飑、风向转变、气温下降。

abstract.en: Picture a wedge driving under a soft layer and lifting it off the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一个楔子钻到柔软层下面，把它整体抬离地面。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn across a map with little teeth pointing one way.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画的一条线，小齿朝一个方向。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that turns cold in a single hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一场对话在一个小时里转冷。

examples.en: The cold front reached the airport before the storm cells did.
examples.cn: 冷锋在雷暴单体之前抵达机场。

examples.en: Pressure rose sharply behind the cold front.
examples.cn: 冷锋之后气压急剧上升。

examples.en: Sailors welcome a cold front in summer and dread it in winter.
examples.cn: 水手夏天欢迎冷锋，冬天却怕它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cold（冷）+ front（前沿）」——冷空气推进的前沿 → 冷锋

root: cold 为古英语 cald「低温」，与德语 kalt、荷兰语 koud 同源；front 经法语出自拉丁 frons, frontis「额头、正面」。短语为 20 世纪初气象学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the advancing edge to the weather of its passage, its steep slope, its cloud line, the clear air behind, a cold outbreak, the chart symbol and finally an abrupt chill between people.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从推进的前沿，走到过境天气、陡峭坡度、云线、锋后晴空、寒潮爆发、天气图符号，最后是人与人之间的骤然冷淡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wedge of dense air driving under a softer layer and lifting it clear.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个密实空气的楔子钻到柔软层下面，把它抬离地面。

branches.en: THE WEDGE: density difference sets both the boundary and its steep slope.
branches.cn: 楔体：密度差同时决定交界与陡坡。

branches.en: PASSAGE: the concentrated lift produces a squall and a narrow cloud line.
branches.cn: 过境：集中抬升产生飑与狭窄云线。

branches.en: AFTERMATH: subsiding cold air clears the sky; a large advance becomes a cold wave.
branches.cn: 后果：下沉冷空气使天转晴；大规模推进成为寒潮。

branches.en: SYMBOL: triangles encode the direction of advance.
branches.cn: 符号：三角形编码推进方向。

branches.en: METAPHOR: only the sudden drop and the separating line remain.
branches.cn: 比喻：只剩骤降与分隔线。

intro.en: Cold front is an English noun phrase made of a native adjective and a Latin-derived noun; its technical family is built with prefixes and compounds.
intro.cn: cold front 是由本族形容词与拉丁来源名词构成的英语名词短语；其技术词族由前缀与复合成分构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin frons, frontis gives front; Latin gelidus and frigus name cold, though English cold itself is native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 frons, frontis 给出 front；拉丁 gelidus 与 frigus 表示冷，但英语 cold 本身是本族词。

items.example: Cold air sank behind the front.
Post-frontal air was dry and clear.
Cold-frontal cloud formed a narrow band.
The passage lasted under an hour.

items.meaning: a storm triggered at the front
items.example: A cold-front thunderstorm closed the road.
items.exampleCN: 一场冷锋雷暴封闭了道路。

items.meaning: a sudden large advance of cold air
items.meaningCN: 冷空气的突然大规模推进
items.example: The cold-air outbreak reached the gulf.
A cold wave followed the front.
items.exampleCN: 冷锋之后来了一次寒潮。

definition_zh: 相比之下；与……形成对照（用于指出两者的明显差异）
definition_en: used to point out a clear difference between two things, facts or situations
core_image: 同一张展台上，左边满杯，右边空杯，两束光颜色相反
scene: 展柜两侧并排放着满杯与空杯，标签说明两者的差别。 The first case held a full cup; in contrast, the second case held an empty one.
sceneCN: 这里取「相比之下」（第 1 个义项：句首或分句间的对比标记）；句意为第一个展柜里是满杯，相比之下第二个展柜里是空杯。

pos.zh: 状语短语：相比之下
介词短语：与……形成对照

senses.title: The sentence-opening contrast marker
senses.definition: placed at the beginning of a clause to announce that what follows differs from what came before
senses.definitionCN: 置于从句开头，宣告接下来的内容与前述不同
senses.example: The coast is humid; in contrast, the interior is dry.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海潮湿；相比之下，内陆干燥。
senses.why: Fronting the phrase turns the whole clause into the second half of a pair, so the reader expects a mirrored point.
senses.whyCN: 把短语提到句首，整个从句就成了成对句的后半，读者自然期待一个对应的点。

senses.title: The mid-sentence pivot
senses.definition: inserted between two parallel statements, often with a semicolon or a comma, to mark the turning point
senses.definitionCN: 插在两个平行陈述之间，常用分号或逗号隔开，标出转折点
senses.example: The first method is cheap; the second, in contrast, is accurate.
senses.exampleCN: 第一种方法便宜；相比之下，第二种精准。
senses.why: In the middle the phrase pivots the sentence without breaking it, which is why it often sits inside commas.
senses.whyCN: 放在中间，短语完成转折却不打断句子，因此常被逗号夹住。

senses.title: A named reference point
senses.titleCN: 后接介词加名词：与……截然不同
senses.definition: used before to and a noun to name the thing that the subject differs from
senses.definitionCN: 用在介词加名词之前，点出主语与之不同的事物
senses.example: In contrast to earlier studies, the new survey found no decline.
senses.exampleCN: 与早先的研究不同，这次调查没有发现下降。
senses.why: To names the standard of comparison, so the phrase stops being an adverb and becomes a prepositional frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个介词点出比较的基准，于是这个短语不再是副词，而成了介词框架。

senses.title: The formal with variant
senses.titleCN: 后接另一个介词加名词：与……相比（正式/英式）
senses.definition: used with with instead of to, chiefly in formal British writing, with the same meaning
senses.definitionCN: 用一个介词代替另一个，多见于正式的英式书面语，意义相同
senses.example: In contrast with the coastal group, the inland group moved less.
senses.exampleCN: 与沿海组相比，内陆组流动更少。
senses.why: The two prepositions are near-variants; with is the older, more formal partner and to the more common modern one.
senses.whyCN: 两个介词近乎变体；一个更旧更正式，另一个是现代更常见的搭档。

senses.title: The academic counter-evidence signal
senses.titleCN: 学术语篇：引出相反证据
senses.definition: in research writing, used to introduce a result that opposes the one just reported
senses.definitionCN: 在学术写作中，用来引出与前一条结果相反的结果
senses.example: The first trial failed; in contrast, the second trial met every target.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次试验失败；相比之下，第二次试验达成了全部目标。
senses.why: Research prose needs a signal that separates two findings without claiming either is wrong, and this phrase supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作需要一个把两项发现分开、又不判定谁错的信号，这个短语正好提供。

senses.title: The paragraph-opening turn
senses.definition: at the start of a paragraph or section, used to shift the discussion to the opposite case
senses.definitionCN: 在段落或章节开头使用，把讨论转向相反的情形
senses.example: In contrast, the following section examines rural households.
senses.exampleCN: 相比之下，下一节考察农村家庭。
senses.why: At paragraph level the phrase is a signpost, telling the reader that the argument is about to switch sides.
senses.whyCN: 在段落层面，这个短语是路标，告诉读者论证即将换边。

senses.title: The parallel-structure contrast
senses.titleCN: 并列结构：同一句中对照两个事实
senses.definition: used in a single sentence to balance two opposite facts, often with parallel wording
senses.definitionCN: 在同一句中平衡两个相反事实，措辞常保持平行
senses.example: Prices rose in the north; in contrast, wages fell in the south.
senses.exampleCN: 北方物价上涨；相比之下，南方工资下降。
senses.why: Parallel clauses make the contrast measurable, and the phrase marks where the second half begins.
senses.whyCN: 平行从句让对比可衡量，短语则标出后半句的起点。

senses.title: The data-description contrast
senses.titleCN: 图表与数据：与前一组数字对照
senses.definition: used when reporting figures to set the current number against an earlier or neighbouring one
senses.definitionCN: 报告数字时，把当前数字与先前或相邻数字并置
senses.example: In contrast, the 2020 figure almost doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 相比之下，2020 年的数字几乎翻了一倍。
senses.why: Numerical writing uses the phrase to keep two series apart without repeating the whole comparison in words.
senses.whyCN: 数字写作借此把两组数据分开，不必用文字重复整个比较。

intro.en: Contrast came into English through French from Italian contrastare, a Vulgar Latin verb built on Latin contra, against, and stare, to stand. The reconstruction is reliable; the date of the English phrase is approximate.
intro.cn: contrast 经法语、意大利语进入英语，其动词是通俗拉丁语形式，由拉丁语 contra「反对」与 stare「站立」构成。该重构形式可靠；英语短语的年代为约数。

items.en: Contra, against, is the same element found in contradiction and contraflow.
items.cn: contra 意为「反对」，与 contradiction、contraflow 中的成分相同。

items.en: Stare, to stand, gives the picture of two things standing face to face.
items.cn: stare 意为「站立」，画出两物面对面站立的画面。

items.en: The reconstructed verb meant to stand against or withstand.
items.cn: 重构的动词意为「对立而站、抵抗」。

items.en: Italian contrastare passed into French as contraster and then into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 意大利语 contrastare 传入法语作 contraster，十六世纪再进入英语。

items.en: The prepositional frame in contrast appears in modern written English; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 介词框架 in contrast 出现在近代书面英语中，确切首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group occupies the same contrast slot but names different relations; the second group holds other connectors that also set two facts against each other.
note.cn: 第一组占同样的对比位置，却指不同的关系；第二组是同样把两件事并置的其他连接语。

entries.definition: It weighs two things on one scale; in contrast stresses that they diverge.
entries.definitionCN: 它把两物放在同一把尺上；本短语强调两者分道扬镳。

entries.definition: It works as a stand-alone connector and rarely takes to or with after it.
entries.definitionCN: 它作独立连接语，很少在后面接介词。

entries.definition: It rejects a stated negative and asserts the opposite; it does not simply set two facts side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 它否定一个被说出的否定命题并主张相反面，不只是把两件事并置。

entries.definition: It concedes an obstacle; it never introduces a second item to compare.
entries.definitionCN: 它承认阻碍，从不引出被比较的第二项。

entries.definition: A conjunction joining two clauses that differ, common in formal and legal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 连接两个不同从句的连词，多见于正式与法律文字。

entries.definition: It marks the reverse side of a relation rather than a mere difference.
entries.definitionCN: 它标出关系的反面，而不只是差异。

entries.definition: It marks what takes the place of something, not a parallel contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 它标出替代物，而非平行对照。

entries.definition: It introduces the second side of an argument in a more conversational tone.
entries.definitionCN: 以更口语的语气引出论点的另一面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pair, the real prepositions and the real position rules.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实拉丁语对、真实介词与真实位置规则。

normal.en: Contra is against and stare is to stand, so two things stand facing each other.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根一是「反」，一是「站」，两物便面对面站着。

normal.en: In contrast to and in contrast with both take a noun, never a clause.
normal.cn: 这个短语的两种介词形式都接名词，从不接从句。

normal.en: At the front it announces the other side; between clauses it pivots.
normal.cn: 句首宣告另一面，句间完成转折。

normal.en: Its twin by contrast usually stands alone and avoids to and with.
normal.cn: 它的近义双胞胎通常独立使用，避开介词。

normal.en: It pairs things; it does not deny what was said, which is the job of on the contrary.
normal.cn: 它把两物配对，并不否定已说的话，那是对立说法的工作。

abstract.en: Like two lamps of opposite colours switched on at the two ends of one table.
abstract.cn: 像同一张桌子两端亮起两盏颜色相反的灯。

abstract.en: Like a hinge in the middle of a sentence, letting the second half swing the other way.
abstract.cn: 像句子中间的一枚铰链，让后半句向另一边转。

abstract.en: Like a scale with one full pan and one empty pan, both visible at once.
abstract.cn: 像一架天平，一端满一端空，同时可见。

examples.en: The north remained industrial; in contrast, the south turned to services.
examples.cn: 北方仍是工业区；相比之下，南方转向服务业。

examples.en: In contrast to the first edition, the second contains almost no illustrations.
examples.cn: 与第一版不同，第二版几乎没有插图。

examples.en: In contrast with the coastal towns, inland villages lost population.
examples.cn: 与沿海城镇相比，内陆村庄人口减少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因 康特拉斯特」——两物面对面站着，一比就看出不同：相比之下

root: contrast 经法语、意大利语进入英语，其动词由拉丁语 contra「反对」与 stare「站立」构成通俗拉丁语重构形式；短语 in contrast 属近代书面英语，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by position and complement: front and mid-clause markers, to and with plus a noun, academic counter-evidence, paragraph signpost, parallel clauses, and figure reporting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按位置与搭配区分：句首与句中的对比标记、两个介词加名词、学术反证、段落路标、平行从句、数字报告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one full cup and one empty cup displayed side by side under opposite lights.
core.cn: 核心意象：满杯与空杯并排摆在相反的灯光下。

branches.en: THE PAIRED CLAUSE: two parallel statements are set face to face.
branches.cn: 成对从句：两个平行陈述面对面摆开。

branches.en: THE HINGE: inserted mid-sentence, the phrase turns without breaking the line.
branches.cn: 铰链：插在句中，转折而不打断句子。

branches.en: THE BENCHMARK: to and with name the thing being stood against.
branches.cn: 基准：两个介词点出被对照的对象。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT SIGNPOST: research and paragraph openings use it to switch sides.
branches.cn: 论证路标：研究与段落开头用它换边。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: in data writing two series are kept apart without repeating the comparison.
branches.cn: 数字：数据写作中把两组数字分开，不重复比较。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin preposition and a Latin verb of standing; the reconstruction belongs to Vulgar Latin.
intro.cn: 这个短语由拉丁语介词与拉丁语「站立」动词组成；重构形式属通俗拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin etyma are contra, against, and stare, to stand; the verb passed through Italian and French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 contra「反对」与 stare「站立」；动词经意大利语与法语传来。

items.example: Contra appears in many English compounds of opposition.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在许多表对立的英语复合词里。

items.example: The verb supplies the image of standing one's ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「站定不退」的画面。

items.example: The reconstructed verb is the missing link between Latin and Italian.
items.exampleCN: 这个重构动词是拉丁语与意大利语之间缺失的一环。

items.example: French carried the verb into English in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 法语在十六世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.example: The noun names the difference that the phrase points to.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名短语所指出的差异。

items.example: The phrase works as a connector in written English.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语在书面英语里作连接语。

items.example: Its twin usually stands alone between sentences.
items.exampleCN: 它的双胞胎通常在句间独立使用。

definition_zh: 板块构造学说；岩石圈板块运动与相互作用的全球理论
definition_en: the theory that the Earth's lithosphere is divided into plates that move and interact
core_image: 一只裂成多块硬壳的球，碎壳漂浮在软层上，彼此挤压、拉开、错动
scene: 地震为什么集中在环太平洋一带，并不是偶然。 The theory of plate tectonics explains why earthquakes cluster along the Pacific rim.
sceneCN: 这里 plate tectonics 指「板块构造学说」（第 1 个义项：解释板块运动与相互作用的全球理论）；句意为板块构造学说解释了地震为何集中在环太平洋一带。

pos.zh: 板块构造（学说）；板块构造学

senses.title: The unifying theory
senses.titleCN: 板块构造学说：统一地质学的理论
senses.definition: the theory that the lithosphere is broken into plates that move over the weaker mantle
senses.definitionCN: 认为岩石圈裂成板块并在较软弱地幔之上运动的理论
senses.example: The theory of plate tectonics explains why earthquakes cluster along the Pacific rim.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造学说解释了地震为何集中在环太平洋一带。
senses.why: The name joins the object (plates) with the field (tectonics), so the phrase literally means the study of how plates are built and moved.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称把对象（板块）与学科（tectonics）合在一起，字面意思就是研究板块如何构成与运动。

senses.title: The process of plate motion
senses.definition: the actual movement and interaction of lithospheric plates
senses.definitionCN: 岩石圈板块实际的移动与相互作用
senses.example: Plate tectonics has been shaping this ocean basin for a hundred million years.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造作用塑造这个大洋盆地已有一亿年。
senses.why: Like tectonics alone, the phrase can name the process as well as the theory that describes it.
senses.whyCN: 与单用的 tectonics 一样，这个短语既可指过程，也可指描述过程的理论。

senses.title: A global framework
senses.definition: the global framework that links earthquakes, volcanoes, mountains and ocean basins
senses.definitionCN: 把地震、火山、山脉与大洋盆地联系起来的全球框架
senses.example: Plate tectonics turned separate observations into one connected story.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造把彼此分离的观察变成一个连贯的故事。
senses.why: The theory's power is unification: one mechanism at plate boundaries explains many surface features.
senses.whyCN: 这个理论的力量在于统一：板块边界上的一种机制解释了许多地表特征。

senses.title: Interaction at plate boundaries
senses.titleCN: 板块边界上的相互作用
senses.definition: the three ways plates meet: spreading, converging and sliding past each other
senses.definitionCN: 板块相接的三种方式：张裂、汇聚与错动
senses.example: Plate tectonics predicts different rock types at different boundary types.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造预言不同类型边界上会出现不同的岩石组合。
senses.why: Every boundary type has a characteristic geometry of stress, so the theory predicts what should form there.
senses.whyCN: 每种边界都有特征性的应力几何，因此理论可以预言那里应当形成什么。

senses.title: The reason for earthquake belts
senses.definition: the explanation of why earthquakes follow narrow belts rather than scattering evenly
senses.definitionCN: 解释地震为何沿狭窄条带分布而非均匀散布
senses.example: Plate tectonics showed that the Pacific ring of fire is a boundary, not a coincidence.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造说明环太平洋火山地震带是一条边界，而不是巧合。
senses.why: Friction and bending concentrate at plate edges, so strain accumulates there and releases as earthquakes.
senses.whyCN: 摩擦与弯折集中在板块边缘，应力在那里积累并以地震方式释放。

senses.title: The mechanism of mountains and rifts
senses.definition: the mechanism by which collisions raise mountains and extension opens rifts
senses.definitionCN: 碰撞抬升山脉、拉伸张开裂谷的机制
senses.example: Plate tectonics links the Himalaya to a collision and the Red Sea to a rift.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造把喜马拉雅山与一次碰撞、把红海与一条裂谷联系起来。
senses.why: Compression thickens the crust and extension thins it, so both mountain belts and rift valleys are boundary products.
senses.whyCN: 挤压使地壳增厚，拉伸使地壳变薄，因此山脉带与裂谷都是板块边界的产物。

senses.title: A tool for reconstructing the past
senses.definition: the use of plate motions to reconstruct the positions of ancient continents
senses.definitionCN: 用板块运动重建古大陆位置的方法
senses.example: Plate tectonics lets geologists place the continents on a map of two hundred million years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 板块构造使地质学家能画出两亿年前大陆的位置。
senses.why: If plates move at measurable rates, their past positions can be run backwards like a film.
senses.whyCN: 如果板块以可测量的速度移动，它们的过去位置就可以像倒放影片一样推算出来。

senses.title: Plate behaviour on other planets
senses.definition: the comparative study of whether other rocky planets have moving plates
senses.definitionCN: 比较研究其他岩石行星是否有运动板块
senses.example: Venus seems to lack plate tectonics, which changes how its heat escapes.
senses.exampleCN: 金星似乎没有板块构造，这改变了它散热的方式。
senses.why: A planet with plates cools differently from one with a single unbroken shell, so the comparison matters.
senses.whyCN: 有板块的行星与只有一整层外壳的行星散热方式不同，因此这种比较很重要。

intro.en: Plate tectonics is a twentieth-century compound of an everyday noun and a Greek-derived field name. Each part has its own history. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: plate tectonics 是二十世纪由日常名词与希腊来源的学科名构成的复合术语。两部分各有自己的历史。年代均为约数。

items.en: The plate element goes back through Old French plate 'thin metal sheet' to Medieval Latin plata and, generally accepted, to Greek platys 'broad, flat'.
items.cn: plate 一词经古法语 plate「薄金属片」上溯到中世纪拉丁语 plata，一般认为再追溯到希腊语 platys「宽而平的」。

items.en: The tectonics element comes from Greek tekton 'builder' and tektonikos 'relating to building'.
items.cn: tectonics 部分来自希腊语 tekton「建造者」与 tektonikos「与建造有关的」。

items.en: Alfred Wegener's continental drift proposed moving landmasses but lacked a convincing mechanism.
items.cn: 阿尔弗雷德·魏格纳的大陆漂移说提出陆块会移动，但缺少令人信服的机制。

items.en: Seafloor spreading supplied the mechanism, and the phrase plate tectonics was adopted for the theory of moving lithospheric plates.
items.cn: 海底扩张提供了机制，plate tectonics 这一说法被用来指岩石圈板块运动的理论。

items.en: The phrase is now the standard name of the unifying theory and is often shortened to tectonics in context.
items.cn: 这个短语现在是这一统一理论的标准名称，在语境中常简称为 tectonics。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from its parts and near neighbours; group two separates it from other theories of the same generation.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与它的组成部分及形近词分开；第二组把它与同一时期的其他理论分开。

entries.definition: the field name alone; plate tectonics is the specific theory of moving plates.
entries.definitionCN: 单用的学科名；plate tectonics 特指板块运动的理论。

entries.definition: the adjective form used before a noun, as in plate tectonic processes.
entries.definitionCN: 作定语时的形容词形式，如 plate tectonic processes（板块构造过程）。

entries.definition: a small blood cell fragment; it shares plate but ends in the diminutive -let.
entries.definitionCN: 血液中的小块细胞碎片；它共享 plate，但结尾是表小的 -let。

entries.definition: a flat elevated area of land; it is a landform, not a theory.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦的高地；它是地貌，不是理论。

entries.definition: the earlier idea that continents moved across the globe; it lacked a mechanism and was absorbed into plate tectonics.
entries.definitionCN: 早期认为大陆会在地球上移动的想法；它缺少机制，后来被板块构造吸收。

entries.definition: the process that creates new ocean floor at ridges; it supplied the mechanism plate tectonics needed.
entries.definitionCN: 在大洋中脊生成新洋底的过程；它为板块构造提供了所需机制。

entries.definition: the sinking of one plate beneath another; it is one part of plate tectonics, not the whole theory.
entries.definitionCN: 一个板块俯冲到另一个板块之下；它是板块构造的一部分，不是整个理论。

entries.definition: mountain building; it is a consequence of plate interaction, not the framework itself.
entries.definitionCN: 造山作用；它是板块相互作用的后果，而不是框架本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the phrase is readable part by part, and each part is a real word with a real history.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个短语可以逐部分读出，而每部分都是真实的词、有真实的历史。

normal.en: plate is the flat slab, tectonics is the building study: plate tectonics is the study of how flat slabs build the Earth's surface.
normal.cn: plate 是平板，tectonics 是建造之学：板块构造就是研究平板如何搭建地球表面。

normal.en: The theory has three boundary types: spreading, converging and sliding, which is why one framework covers so much.
normal.cn: 这个理论有三种边界：张裂、汇聚与错动，所以一个框架能覆盖很多现象。

normal.en: Continental drift was the proposal; seafloor spreading was the mechanism; plate tectonics was the full theory.
normal.cn: 大陆漂移是提法，海底扩张是机制，板块构造是完整的理论。

normal.en: The ring of fire is a plate boundary, which is why the phrase explains earthquake belts.
normal.cn: 环太平洋火山地震带是一条板块边界，所以这个短语能解释地震带。

normal.en: Plates move a few centimetres a year, about as fast as a fingernail grows.
normal.cn: 板块每年移动几厘米，大约和指甲生长一样快。

abstract.en: Abstractly, plate tectonics is a system of moving pieces: the whole surface is a puzzle whose pieces exchange material.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，板块构造是一个运动碎块的系统：整个表面是一幅拼图，碎块之间交换物质。

abstract.en: Its lesson is that large slow motion produces sudden events: centimeters per year become earthquakes in seconds.
abstract.cn: 它给出的启示是缓慢的大运动产生突发事件：每年几厘米的位移会在几秒内变成地震。

abstract.en: Symbol: a cracked shell with arrows pointing apart, together and sideways at three different seams.
abstract.cn: 符号：一层裂开的壳，三条不同的接缝上分别画着分开、合拢与侧向的箭头。

examples.en: Plate tectonics revolutionized geology in the nineteen sixties.
examples.cn: 板块构造学说在二十世纪六十年代彻底改变了地质学。

examples.en: The Alps formed through plate tectonics as two landmasses collided.
examples.cn: 阿尔卑斯山是两块陆地在板块构造作用下碰撞形成的。

examples.en: Without plate tectonics, the planet would lose heat in a very different way.
examples.cn: 如果没有板块构造，这颗行星散热的方式会大不相同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「平板 + 构造」—— 地球的硬壳像打碎的平板，一块块挪动 → plate tectonics 板块构造

root: plate 源自希腊语 platys（宽平的），tectonics 源自希腊语 tekton（建造者），合指「平板如何搭建地表」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of plate tectonics. The thread runs from the theory, to the process, to the boundaries, and out to other planets.
sensesIntro.cn: plate tectonics 的八个义项。主线从理论，到过程，到边界，再延伸到其他行星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cracked shell whose pieces move on a soft base.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层裂开的硬壳，碎块在软层上移动。

branches.en: THEORY: one framework unifies scattered surface features.
branches.cn: 理论：一个框架统一了散落的地表特征。

branches.en: PROCESS AND BOUNDARY: motion happens where plates meet, spread or slide.
branches.cn: 过程与边界：运动发生在板块相接、张裂或错动之处。

branches.en: CONSEQUENCES: strain at edges produces earthquakes, mountains and rifts.
branches.cn: 后果：边缘的应力产生地震、山脉与裂谷。

branches.en: TIME DEPTH: measurable motion can be run backwards to reconstruct the past.
branches.cn: 时间深度：可测量的运动可以倒推，用来重建过去。

branches.en: COMPARISON: the theory becomes a test of whether other planets have plates.
branches.cn: 比较：这个理论也成为检验其他行星是否有板块的标准。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Germanic-rooted everyday noun with a Greek-derived field name, and each part builds its own compounds.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个日常名词与一个希腊来源的学科名组合起来，两部分各自都能构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Plate reached English through Old French and Medieval Latin from Greek platys 'flat'; tectonics came through Latin tectonicus from Greek tekton 'builder'. The two halves have separate histories.
latinIntro.cn: plate 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语上溯到希腊语 platys「平的」；tectonics 经拉丁语 tectonicus 上溯到希腊语 tekton「建造者」。两半各有独立的历史。

items.structure: Greek platys 'flat' → Latin plata → Old French plate
items.example: The plate is a rigid slab of lithosphere.
items.exampleCN: 板块是岩石圈的一块刚性平板。

items.meaning: the study of structure and construction
items.meaningCN: 研究结构与建造的学科
items.example: Tectonics explains how the crust is assembled.
items.exampleCN: 构造学研究地壳如何组装。

items.meaning: the edge where two plates meet
items.example: Most volcanoes sit near a plate boundary.
items.exampleCN: 大多数火山位于板块边界附近。

items.example: Plate motion is measured by satellite signals.
items.exampleCN: 板块运动用卫星信号测量。

items.meaning: relating to the theory or its processes
items.meaningCN: 与板块构造理论或过程有关的
items.example: Plate-tectonic models predict where strain accumulates.
items.exampleCN: 板块构造模型预测应力在哪里积累。

items.meaning: another name for a plate boundary
items.meaningCN: 板块边界的另一种说法
items.example: The margin is the most active part of the plate.
items.exampleCN: 边缘是板块最活跃的部分。

items.meaning: a small plate within a larger system
items.example: A microplate rotates between two larger plates.
items.exampleCN: 一个小板块在两个较大板块之间旋转。

items.meaning: a minor plate below or within a larger one
items.meaningCN: 位于较大板块之下或内部的小板块
items.example: The subplate carries a small volcanic chain.
items.exampleCN: 这个小板块上带着一条小火山链。

definition_zh: 提倡者；拥护者；（苏格兰法）出庭辩护人
definition_en: a person who publicly supports a cause or policy; in Scots law, a pleader admitted to practise before the higher courts
core_image: 被叫到你身边、替你出声的那个人
scene: 会场后排有人站起来，一遍遍替那条提案说话。 He was a lifelong advocator of free public libraries.
sceneCN: 这里 advocator 是「提倡者」（第 1 个义项：公开支持某项事业或主张的人）；句意为他一生都是免费公共图书馆的提倡者。核心画面是有人被叫到你身边替你出声。

pos.zh: 提倡者；拥护者；辩护人

become an advocator of the plan
