definition_zh: 爬行动物的；像爬行动物的；冷酷阴险的
definition_en: relating to or resembling reptiles, or cold and unemotional like a reptile
core_image: 特写中一只蜥蜴的竖瞳在冷光下缩成细缝，毫无表情
scene: 特写镜头里，蜥蜴的竖瞳在冷光中缩成一条细缝，一动不动。 The reptilian eye narrowed to a vertical slit in the cold light.
sceneCN: 这里 reptilian 指「爬行动物般的」（第 1 个义项：属于或类似爬行动物的）；句意为那只爬行动物般的眼睛在冷光中缩成一条竖缝。

pos.zh: 爬行动物的；像爬行动物的；冷酷的
爬行类生物；似爬行类的人形生物（科幻用法）

collocations.zh: 爬行动物脑（原始本能层面的比喻）

derivatives.zh: 似爬行类生物（科幻复数）

senses.title: Relating to reptiles
senses.definition: of, relating to, or belonging to reptiles
senses.definitionCN: 属于、关于或与爬行动物有关的
senses.example: The reptilian eye narrowed to a vertical slit.
senses.exampleCN: 那只爬行动物般的眼睛缩成一条竖缝。
senses.why: The suffix -ian turns the noun reptile into a relational adjective, so reptilian answers 'of what group?'
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ian 把名词 reptile 变成表关系的形容词，因此 reptilian 回答「属于哪一类」。

senses.title: Having reptile-like physical traits
senses.titleCN: 具有爬行动物般的外形特征
senses.definition: showing scales, dry skin, a low stance or a cold, fixed gaze
senses.definitionCN: 呈现鳞片、干燥皮肤、低伏姿态或冷硬不动的凝视
senses.example: The mask gave him a reptilian appearance.
senses.exampleCN: 那张面具让他看起来像爬行动物。
senses.why: The adjective extends from real reptiles to anything that looks like one, so scales and stillness become the visual cues.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从真实爬行动物扩展到任何看起来像爬行动物的东西，鳞片与静止便成了视觉线索。

senses.title: Cold and unemotional
senses.definition: describing a person or behaviour seen as cold, calculating and unfeeling
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人或行为冷酷、算计、没有感情
senses.example: He answered with a reptilian calm that unsettled the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他以一种爬行动物般的冷静作答，让全场不安。
senses.why: The figurative sense borrows the reptile's reputed coldness and lack of expression, turning biology into a moral judgement.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义借用了爬行动物「冷血」与「无表情」的名声，把生物学变成道德评判。

senses.title: The 'reptilian brain' in popular science
senses.titleCN: 通俗科学中的「爬行动物脑」
senses.definition: a popular term for primitive, instinct-driven brain functions, supposed to resemble the reptile brain
senses.definitionCN: 通俗术语，指原始的、由本能驱动的脑功能，据说类似爬行动物的脑
senses.example: The reptilian brain is said to handle fear and territory.
senses.exampleCN: 所谓爬行动物脑被认为负责恐惧与领地。
senses.why: The triune-brain model gave ancient instincts a reptilian label; the term is a metaphor, not an anatomical finding.
senses.whyCN: 「三层脑」模型给古老本能贴上爬行动物标签；这个说法是比喻，并非解剖学结论。

senses.title: A reptilian fossil assemblage
senses.definition: used of a fossil fauna made up chiefly of reptile remains
senses.definitionCN: 用于指主要由爬行动物遗骸构成的化石动物群
senses.example: The reptilian fauna of the red beds includes several dinosaurs.
senses.exampleCN: 红层的爬行动物群包括好几种恐龙。
senses.why: Palaeontology needs an adjective to describe a whole assemblage, where 'reptile' would suggest a single animal.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学需要形容词来描述整个组合，用名词 reptile 会让人以为指单个动物。

senses.title: Of the reptile lineage
senses.definition: belonging to the evolutionary lineage that includes reptiles and, in modern classification, birds
senses.definitionCN: 属于包含爬行动物、现代分类中还包括鸟类的演化支
senses.example: Birds are reptilian in the strict evolutionary sense.
senses.exampleCN: 从严格的演化意义上说，鸟类属于爬行类支系。
senses.why: Modern phylogeny puts birds inside the reptile tree, so the adjective can describe a lineage rather than a body plan.
senses.whyCN: 现代系统发生学把鸟类放在爬行类树内，因此这个形容词可以描述演化支，而非身体形态。

senses.title: A reptile-like being in fiction
senses.titleCN: 科幻中的似爬行类生物
senses.definition: a fictional humanoid or alien with reptile features
senses.definitionCN: 具有爬行动物特征的虚构人形或外星生物
senses.example: The reptilian in the film spoke with two voices.
senses.exampleCN: 影片中的似爬行类生物用两种声音说话。
senses.why: Fiction uses the adjective as a noun because the creature is not a real reptile but only resembles one.
senses.whyCN: 虚构作品把这个形容词用作名词，因为该生物不是真实爬行动物，只是相似。

senses.title: Reptile leather goods
senses.definition: made from the skin of snakes, crocodiles or other reptiles
senses.definitionCN: 由蛇、鳄或其他爬行动物皮革制成的
senses.example: The shop sold reptilian belts and bags.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖爬行动物皮革的腰带与包。
senses.why: The material trade prefers the adjective because it modifies the product noun, as in reptilian leather.
senses.whyCN: 材料行业偏好用形容词，因为它修饰产品名词，如 reptilian leather。

intro.en: Reptilian is Latin reptilis 'creeping' plus the suffix -ian; the adjective was formed in English on the noun reptile. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reptilian 由拉丁 reptilis「爬行的」加后缀 -ian 构成；这个形容词是在英语中依名词 reptile 造出的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Reptilis meant 'creeping', from repere 'to creep'. The verb's deeper origin is unsettled, so any earlier root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: reptilis 意为「爬行的」，来自 repere「爬行」。该动词的更深来源没有定论，凡更早的词根都属重构。

items.en: The suffix -ian, from Latin -ianus through French, forms adjectives of belonging, as in mammalian and amphibian.
items.cn: 后缀 -ian 经法语来自拉丁 -ianus，构成表归属的形容词，如 mammalian 与 amphibian。

items.en: English reptilian appears in the nineteenth century, when zoology needed a relational adjective beside the noun reptile.
items.cn: 英语 reptilian 在 19 世纪出现，当时动物学需要一个与名词 reptile 相配的关系形容词。

items.en: By the later nineteenth century the adjective was applied to cold, unblinking people as well as to animals.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪后期，这个形容词除了动物，也用于形容冷酷、不眨眼的人。

items.en: The phrase 'reptilian brain' spread in the 1960s with the triune-brain model; it is a popular metaphor, not a literal description of human anatomy.
items.cn: reptilian brain 一说随 1960 年代的「三层脑」模型流行；它是通俗比喻，并非对人体解剖的写实描述。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Latin and suffix stages are clear, but repere's pre-Latin origin is unsettled and the first English use is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：拉丁与后缀阶段清楚，但 repere 的拉丁语之前来源没有定论，英语首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same reptile family; group two holds adjectives for the cold or scaly quality that reptilian also conveys.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 reptile 词族的形式；第二组是同样传达「冷」或「有鳞」质感的形容词。

entries.definition: The animal itself; reptilian is the adjective and cannot replace it as a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 动物本身；reptilian 是形容词，不能作主语代替它。

entries.definition: The formal Latin class; reptilian describes anything belonging to or resembling it.
entries.definitionCN: 正式拉丁纲名；reptilian 描述属于或类似该纲的事物。

entries.definition: A botanical adjective for creeping stems; it shares the Latin verb but is not used of animals.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学形容词，指匍匐茎；同出拉丁动词，但不用于动物。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', it stresses resemblance without membership, whereas reptilian can mean either.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，强调相似而非归属；reptilian 则两种意思都可。

entries.definition: Literally describing an animal that depends on external heat, figuratively describing a cruel person; reptilian leans on the figurative side.
entries.definitionCN: 字面指依赖外部热量的动物，比喻指残忍的人；reptilian 更偏比喻一面。

entries.definition: Of or like lizards, from Greek sauros 'lizard'; it is narrower than reptilian and suggests a lizard shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指蜥蜴的或像蜥蜴的，来自希腊 sauros「蜥蜴」；比 reptilian 窄，暗示蜥蜴形态。

entries.definition: Snake-like in movement or form; it stresses winding motion, which reptilian does not.
entries.definitionCN: 在动作或形态上像蛇；强调蜿蜒运动，而 reptilian 不含此意。

entries.definition: A technical word for scaled reptiles such as snakes and lizards; it is a taxonomic category, not a description of mood.
entries.definitionCN: 指蛇、蜥蜴等有鳞爬行动物的技术词；它是分类范畴，不描述情绪。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: reptile + -ian: the adjective of the reptile group.
normal.cn: reptile + -ian：爬行动物类群的形容词。

normal.en: Reptilian eye and reptilian calm both use the same cold, unblinking image.
normal.cn: reptilian eye 与 reptilian calm 用的是同一个「冷而不用眨」的形象。

normal.en: The reptilian brain is a popular metaphor from the triune-brain model, not a real brain part.
normal.cn: reptilian brain 是「三层脑」模型带来的通俗比喻，不是真实存在的脑区。

normal.en: In modern phylogeny birds are reptilian, even though they do not look like lizards.
normal.cn: 现代系统发生学中鸟类属于爬行类支系，尽管它们看起来不像蜥蜴。

normal.en: Reptiloid says 'looks like'; reptilian says 'belongs to or looks like'.
normal.cn: reptiloid 只说「像」；reptilian 则兼指「属于」与「像」。

abstract.en: Picture a gaze that never blinks and never gives anything away.
abstract.cn: 想象一道从不眨眼、也从不流露任何东西的目光。

abstract.en: Picture an ancient instinct wearing a lizard's face.
abstract.cn: 想象一种古老本能长着一张蜥蜴的脸。

abstract.en: Picture a bird that is, in the family tree, a reptile with feathers.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟，在家谱上其实是一只长了羽毛的爬行动物。

examples.en: The lizard's reptilian skin keeps water loss to a minimum.
examples.cn: 蜥蜴的爬行动物皮肤把水分散失降到最低。

examples.en: His reptilian stare made the interview feel like an interrogation.
examples.cn: 他那爬行动物般的凝视让采访像审讯。

examples.en: The film's reptilian villains were entirely computer-generated.
examples.cn: 片中那些似爬行类的反派完全由电脑生成。

dict_mnemonic.text: reptile（爬行动物）+ ian（的）——爬行动物的；想到竖瞳与冷光，就记住「像爬行动物般冷酷」

root: 拉丁 reptilis「爬行的」（来自 repere「爬行」）+ 后缀 -ian；repere 的更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one cold, scaly image from zoology to metaphor: the group adjective, the physical look, emotional coldness, the 'reptilian brain', fossil faunas, the evolutionary lineage, fictional beings and leather goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个冷而有鳞的形象从动物学走向比喻：类群形容词、外形、情感冷酷、「爬行动物脑」、化石动物群、演化支、虚构生物与皮革制品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vertical slit pupil in cold light, motionless and unreadable.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷光中的一条竖瞳，静止而读不出情绪。

branches.en: MEMBERSHIP: the adjective marks belonging, whether to the class or to its evolutionary lineage.
branches.cn: 归属：形容词标记归属，无论指纲还是指演化支。

branches.en: SURFACE: scales and skins are the visible, tradeable side of the word.
branches.cn: 表面：鳞与皮是这个词可见、可交易的一面。

branches.en: TEMPERAMENT: coldness of body becomes coldness of feeling.
branches.cn: 性情：身体的冷变成情感的冷。

branches.en: INSTINCT: popular science gives ancient drives a reptile label.
branches.cn: 本能：通俗科学给古老驱力贴上爬行动物标签。

branches.en: DEEP AND IMAGINED: fossil beds and invented aliens both wear the adjective.
branches.cn: 深时与想象：化石层与虚构外星生物都披着这个形容词。

intro.en: Reptilian is a transparent derivative of reptile, built with the productive suffix -ian; the stem itself goes back to a Latin verb.
intro.cn: reptilian 是 reptile 的透明派生词，由能产后缀 -ian 构成；词干本身可上溯到拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin repere 'to creep' gives reptilis and reptilium; English draws reptile, reptilian and reptant from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 repere「爬行」衍生 reptilis 与 reptilium；英语的 reptile、reptilian、reptant 同出这一词族。

items.example: The stem carries the low, creeping motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着低伏爬行的动作。

items.example: The suffix makes the group adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成类群形容词。

items.meaningCN: 爬行动物的；像爬行动物的
items.exampleCN: 那只爬行动物般的眼睛从不眨。

items.example: The story is full of reptilians.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事里满是似爬行类生物。

items.example: A reptile warmed itself on the stone.
items.exampleCN: 一只爬行动物在石上取暖。

items.example: The reptant stem spread across the ground.
The mask had a reptiloid shape.
items.exampleCN: 面具呈似爬行动物的形状。

definition_zh: 无政府状态；混乱；无秩序
definition_en: a state of society without government or order; complete confusion and disorder
core_image: 没人管的红绿灯路口：车流横冲直撞，乱成一团
scene: 停电整夜后，这座城市的十字路口没人指挥。 After the power cut, the crossroads fell into complete anarchy, with cars honking from every direction.
sceneCN: 这里的 anarchy 是「混乱、无秩序」（第 2 个义项：彻底的混乱）；句意是停电后十字路口彻底失序，各个方向的汽车都在按喇叭。

pos.zh: 无政府状态；混乱；无秩序

derivatives.zh: 由 anarchy 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「无政府的；混乱无序的」
由 anarchy 加施动者后缀 -ist 构成，义为「无政府主义者」
由 anarchy 加后缀 -ism 构成，义为「无政府主义（政治学说）」

senses.title: A society without government
senses.definition: a situation in a country or organization where there is no government, no authority, or no system of control
senses.definitionCN: 国家或组织中没有政府、没有权威、没有管理体系的局面
senses.example: The collapse of the government left the country in anarchy.
senses.exampleCN: 政府垮台使这个国家陷入无政府状态。
senses.why: The Greek prefix an- means without and arkhos means ruler, so the original sense is literally the absence of a ruler.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语前缀 an- 表示「没有」，arkhos 表示「统治者」，本义就是字面上的「没有统治者」，即无政府状态。

senses.title: Complete confusion and disorder
senses.definition: a situation of total confusion where nobody is in control and normal rules do not work
senses.definitionCN: 彻底混乱、无人掌控、正常规则失效的局面
senses.example: The classroom descended into anarchy when the teacher left.
senses.exampleCN: 老师一离开，教室就乱成了一锅粥。
senses.why: When no ruler or rule remains, ordinary activities lose all order, so the word extends from politics to any kind of chaos.
senses.whyCN: 没有了管理者与规则，日常活动便失去一切秩序，于是词义从政治领域扩展到任何混乱场面。

senses.title: Absence of authority between groups
senses.definition: in political theory, the condition in which no higher authority exists above independent states or groups
senses.definitionCN: 政治理论中，指独立国家或群体之上不存在更高权威的状态
senses.example: International relations are often described as an anarchy of sovereign states.
senses.exampleCN: 国际关系常被描述为主权国家之间的无法度状态。
senses.why: Political theorists took the literal meaning, no world ruler over states, and made it a technical term of the discipline.
senses.whyCN: 政治理论家取其字面义「没有一个凌驾各国之上的统治者」，将其变成学科术语，用于描述国际体系。

senses.title: The ideal of a stateless society
senses.definition: the political ideal of a society organized voluntarily without a state or coercive authority
senses.definitionCN: 指一种政治理想：社会在没有国家或强制权威的情况下自愿组织运转
senses.example: Some thinkers believed that anarchy could be a just and peaceful order.
senses.exampleCN: 一些思想家认为无政府状态可以是公正而和平的秩序。
senses.why: Anarchists read the absence of a ruler not as chaos but as freedom, turning the neutral condition into a positive ideal.
senses.whyCN: 无政府主义者把「没有统治者」不是读作混乱而是读作自由，于是把这个中性状态变成了正面的政治理想。

intro.en: Anarchy comes from Greek anarkhia, built on an- without and arkhos ruler.
intro.cn: anarchy 来自希腊语 anarkhia，由 an-（没有）加 arkhos（统治者）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *arkh- meant to begin or to lead, later to rule.
items.cn: 重构词根 *arkh- 表示「开始、带头」，后引申为「统治」。

items.en: Greek arkhos meant ruler, and the prefix an- negated it, giving anarkhos, without a ruler; the abstract noun was anarkhia.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhos 意为「统治者」，前缀 an- 加以否定得 anarkhos「无统治者的」，抽象名词为 anarkhia。

items.en: Plato and other writers used anarkhia both for the absence of magistrates and for disorder in a city.
items.cn: 柏拉图等作家用 anarkhia 兼指「官员缺位」与「城邦的混乱」两种情形。

items.en: The word passed through Latin anarchia and French anarchie before entering English.
items.cn: 该词经拉丁语 anarchia 与法语 anarchie 传入英语。

items.en: English anarchy first appears in the 1530s, describing states without lawful rule.
items.cn: 英语 anarchy 最早见于 1530 年代，用于描述缺乏合法统治的国家状态。

items.en: In the 19th century the word also named the political doctrine of anarchism, which sought a society without a state.
items.cn: 19 世纪起，该词也用于指称无政府主义学说，即主张建立无国家社会的政治思想。

note.en: Anarchy is often confused with anarchism, and contrasted with order and government.
note.cn: anarchy 常与 anarchism 混淆，并与 order、government 形成对照。

entries.definition: the political doctrine that opposes the state
entries.definitionCN: 无政府主义，由 anarchy 加 -ism 构成的学说名称

entries.definition: a person who believes in abolishing government
entries.definitionCN: 无政府主义者，指持有该主张的人

entries.definition: rule by one person such as a king or queen
entries.definitionCN: 君主制，与 anarchy 共用希腊语词根 arkhos（统治者），前缀相反

entries.definition: rule by a small group of people
entries.definitionCN: 寡头统治，同以 arkhos 为词根，指少数人掌权

entries.definition: complete disorder and confusion
entries.definitionCN: 混沌、混乱，强调毫无结构，不带政治含义

entries.definition: a state without laws being obeyed
entries.definitionCN: 无法无天的状态，强调法律不被遵守

entries.definition: a lack of order or organization
entries.definitionCN: 紊乱、无序，语气较弱，泛指秩序缺失

entries.definition: a state of great disturbance and confusion
entries.definitionCN: 骚乱、动荡，强调激烈的动荡感

entries.definition: an organized and controlled condition
entries.definitionCN: 秩序，是 anarchy 混乱义项的直接反义

normalIntro.en: Break anarchy into an- and arkhos to remember its Greek shape.
normalIntro.cn: 把 anarchy 拆成 an- 和 arkhos 来记住它的希腊语结构。

normal.en: an- means without, as in anonymous, without a name.
normal.cn: 前缀 an- 表示「没有」，如 anonymous「匿名的」就是「没有名字」。

normal.en: arkhos means ruler, the same root seen in monarchy.
normal.cn: 词根 arkhos 表示「统治者」，monarchy（君主制）用的就是它。

normal.en: So anarchy literally means without a ruler.
normal.cn: 所以 anarchy 字面意思就是「没有统治者」。

normal.en: Compare monarchy, oligarchy, hierarchy: all name systems of rule.
normal.cn: 对比 monarchy、oligarchy、hierarchy：都以 -archy 结尾，命名各种统治体系。

normal.en: anarchic is the adjective, as in an anarchic classroom.
normal.cn: anarchic 是形容词，如 an anarchic classroom「乱哄哄的课堂」。

abstract.en: Picture a traffic light gone dark: everyone drives as they please.
abstract.cn: 想象红绿灯全灭：人人想怎么开就怎么开。

abstract.en: See an empty throne and a crowd with no one to obey.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空王座，人群无人可服从。

abstract.en: Feel a classroom after the teacher vanishes: papers fly, voices rise.
abstract.cn: 感受老师消失后的教室：纸片乱飞、人声鼎沸。

examples.en: The empire collapsed into anarchy after the emperor was deposed.
examples.cn: 皇帝被废黜后，帝国陷入无政府状态。

examples.en: Without clear rules, the meeting dissolved into anarchy.
examples.cn: 没有明确规则，会议乱成了一团。

examples.en: Critics warned that the new policy would create anarchy in the market.
examples.cn: 批评者警告新政策会造成市场失序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿那惧」——阿婆那都不敢管，谁也不惧权威，没了统治者就是无政府状态：anarchy。

root: 希腊语前缀 an-（没有，元音前否定形式）+ 词根 arkh-（开始、统治，arkhos 统治者）→ anarkhos「无统治者的」→ anarkhia「无统治状态」。同族词 monarchy（君主制）、oligarchy（寡头制）、hierarchy（等级制）。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from the literal absence of a ruler, through general disorder, to the technical and the ideal uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从字面的「没有统治者」出发，经泛化的「混乱」，延伸到政治理论的术语义与无政府主义的理想义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: no ruler, no rules, everyone on their own
core.cn: 核心意象：没有统治者，没有规则，人人自行其是

branches.en: A society literally without a government
branches.cn: 字面上的无政府社会状态

branches.en: Everyday chaos when nobody is in control
branches.cn: 无人掌控时日常生活的混乱

branches.en: States facing each other with no higher power
branches.cn: 各国之上没有更高权威的国际格局

branches.en: Reading the absence of the state as an ideal
branches.cn: 把国家的缺席读作政治理想

branches.en: From missing government to total confusion
branches.cn: 从政府缺位滑向彻底混乱的引申路径

intro.en: Anarchy is built on the Greek root arkhos plus the negative prefix an-.
intro.cn: anarchy 由希腊语词根 arkhos 加否定前缀 an- 构成。

latinIntro.en: The -archy family names systems of rule; Greek roots combine with different prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: -archy 词族命名各种统治体系；希腊语词根搭配不同前缀构成新词。

items.meaning: a person who believes or practices

definition_zh: 寄生；寄生关系；靠他人供养的生存方式
definition_en: the relationship or way of life in which one organism lives at the expense of another
core_image: 两种生物并列：一方贴附在另一方身上，养分的箭头只朝一个方向流动
scene: 这里指「寄生」。 Parasitism keeps the worm alive while slowly weakening the host.
sceneCN: 这里 parasitism 是「寄生关系」（第 1 个义项：一方受益、一方受损的种间关系）；句意：寄生关系让蠕虫存活，同时慢慢削弱宿主。图中可辨识物件：两种生物、单向的养分箭头、逐渐虚弱的宿主轮廓。

pos.zh: 寄生；寄生关系（不可数名词，也可加限定语指某一种寄生类型）

derivatives.zh: 超寄生（寄生物又被寄生的现象）

senses.title: The Biological Relationship
senses.titleCN: 寄生关系：一方受益、一方受损
senses.definition: a close relationship in which one organism benefits and the other is harmed
senses.definitionCN: 一种一方获益、另一方受损的密切种间关系
senses.example: Parasitism differs from mutualism because only one partner gains.
senses.exampleCN: 寄生与互利共生不同，因为只有一方获益。
senses.why: The suffix -ism names a system or relationship rather than an actor. Parasitism is the arrangement itself: one lives in or on the other and takes from it, while the host pays a cost.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 命名的是制度或关系，而不是行动者；parasitism 指这种安排本身：一方生活在他者体表或体内并从中索取，而宿主付出代价。

senses.title: Social Parasitism
senses.titleCN: 社会寄生：人与人之间的单向索取
senses.definition: a social pattern in which one person lives at others' expense
senses.definitionCN: 一个人靠他人供养而生活的社会模式
senses.example: The novel treats parasitism among relatives as a quiet form of violence.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把亲属间的社会寄生当作一种无声的暴力。
senses.why: The oldest English sense of parasite was a social one, a flatterer at a rich man's table. Parasitism extends that picture from a body to a household or a class.
senses.whyCN: parasite 在英语中最古老的义项是社会性的，指在富人家桌旁蹭饭的奉承者；parasitism 把这个画面从身体扩展到家庭或阶层。

senses.title: Brood Parasitism
senses.titleCN: 巢寄生：把养育成本转给别的鸟
senses.definition: the habit of laying eggs in another bird's nest so that the host raises the young
senses.definitionCN: 把蛋产进别的鸟巢、让宿主代为育雏的习性
senses.example: Brood parasitism lets the female avoid all parental care.
senses.exampleCN: 巢寄生让雌鸟完全免去育雏之责。
senses.why: Here the cost transferred is parental care, not food from a body. The relationship is still parasitic because one side pays and the other takes, which is why it is named after the same root.
senses.whyCN: 这里转移的成本是育雏，而不是从身体取食；这段关系仍属寄生，因为一方付账、一方索取，所以沿用同一个词根来命名。

senses.title: Obligate Parasitism
senses.titleCN: 专性寄生：离开宿主就活不了
senses.definition: a form of parasitism in which the parasite cannot complete its life cycle without a host
senses.definitionCN: 寄生物离开宿主便无法完成生活史的寄生形式
senses.example: Obligate parasitism ties the worm's entire cycle to a single host species.
senses.exampleCN: 专性寄生把这种蠕虫的整个生活史绑在单一宿主物种上。
senses.why: Obligate marks necessity. The parasite has lost the ability to live freely, so the host is not an option but a condition of existence. The word measures how deep the dependence has gone.
senses.whyCN: 专性标记「必需」：寄生物已失去自由生活的能力，宿主不是可选项，而是存在的条件；这个词衡量的是依赖深到了什么程度。

senses.title: Facultative Parasitism
senses.titleCN: 兼性寄生：可以寄生，也可以自活
senses.definition: a form of parasitism in which the organism can also live freely
senses.definitionCN: 生物既能寄生、也能自由生活的寄生形式
senses.example: Facultative parasitism allows the fungus to survive in soil between infections.
senses.exampleCN: 兼性寄生让这种真菌在两次感染之间能在土壤中存活。
senses.why: Facultative means optional. The same organism may take a host when it suits it and live independently otherwise, so the relationship is real but not mandatory.
senses.whyCN: 兼性意味着可选：同一生物在合适时可以利用宿主，否则独立生活；因此这段关系真实存在，但不是必需的。

senses.title: Hyperparasitism
senses.titleCN: 超寄生：寄生物又被寄生
senses.definition: the condition in which a parasite is itself parasitised by another organism
senses.definitionCN: 寄生物本身又被另一种生物寄生的状态
senses.example: Hyperparasitism adds a third level to the food chain.
senses.exampleCN: 超寄生给食物链又加上了第三层。
senses.why: Hyper- means 'above, beyond'. The prefix stacks one parasitic relationship on another, producing a chain of hosts in which each level lives at the expense of the one below.
senses.whyCN: hyper- 意为「在上、超出」；这个前缀把一段寄生关系叠在另一段之上，形成一条宿主链，每一层都靠下面一层供养。

senses.title: The Rate of Infection
senses.definition: the proportion of hosts in a population that carry parasites
senses.definitionCN: 一个种群中携带寄生物的宿主所占比例
senses.example: Parasitism reached eighty percent in the sampled snails.
senses.exampleCN: 在抽样的螺中，寄生率达到百分之八十。
senses.why: In ecology the abstract noun can be measured: how many hosts are infected. The sense shifts from the relationship to its frequency, which is what a field study reports.
senses.whyCN: 在生态学中，这个抽象名词可以被测量：有多少宿主被感染；义项从关系本身转向它的出现频率，这正是野外研究要报告的东西。

senses.title: An Evolutionary Strategy
senses.titleCN: 演化策略：一种生存路线
senses.definition: parasitism viewed as an evolutionary strategy for obtaining resources
senses.definitionCN: 把寄生视为获取资源的一种演化策略
senses.example: Parasitism evolved independently in many unrelated groups.
senses.exampleCN: 寄生在许多互不相关的类群中独立演化出来。
senses.why: Evolutionary biology treats parasitism as a route, not only a state: giving up independent resource use can be a successful way to survive. The word then names a strategy rather than a single relationship.
senses.whyCN: 演化生物学把寄生当作一条路线，而不只是一种状态：放弃独立获取资源，可能是一种成功的生存方式；此时这个词命名的是一种策略，而不是某段具体关系。

intro.en: Parasitism is the abstract noun of parasite, formed with -ism. English used it of people for two centuries before biology gave it a precise meaning in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: parasitism 是 parasite 的抽象名词，由 -ism 构成；英语把它用于人长达两个世纪，直到十九世纪生物学才赋予它精确含义。

items.en: Greek parasitos meant 'one who eats at another's table', from para- 'beside' and sitos 'food'. The word named a flatterer who lived at a rich man's expense.
items.cn: 希腊 parasitos 意为「在别人餐桌上吃饭的人」，由 para-「在旁边」与 sitos「食物」构成；这个词指靠富人供养的奉承者。

items.en: Greek -ismos and Latin -ismus formed nouns for practices, systems and doctrines. Added to parasite, it creates the name of the practice rather than the name of the practitioner.
items.cn: 希腊 -ismos 与拉丁 -ismus 构成表示做法、制度与学说的名词；加在 parasite 上，它造出做法之名，而不是从业者之名。

items.en: Parasitism is recorded from the 1610s with the sense 'a habitual living on or at the expense of another'. The first users were describing people, not worms.
items.cn: parasitism 记录于十七世纪十年代，义为「习惯性地靠他人供养生活」；最早的使用者描述的是人，不是蠕虫。

items.en: The biological sense 'vital relation of a parasite to a host' is recorded by 1840. It arrived when naturalists began to classify the many ways in which one organism can live off another.
items.cn: 「寄生物与宿主的生命关系」这一生物学义项记录于 1840 年；它出现于博物学者开始对「一种生物靠另一种生物生活」的多种方式进行分类之时。

items.en: Greek sitos 'grain, food' is of unknown origin, possibly a loanword or substrate word. Beekes's suggestion of a link to a root meaning 'to strike' is disputed. The prefix para- is clear; only the food element is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊 sitos「谷物、食物」来源不确定，可能是借词或底层词；Beekes 提出与意为「击打」的词根有关，但仍有争议。前缀 para- 是清楚的，只有「食物」这一成分存疑。

items.en: Obligate, facultative, brood and hyperparasitism are later technical compounds. Each adds a Latin or Greek modifier to the same abstract noun, marking degree, host or level.
items.cn: 专性、兼性、巢与超寄生都是后来形成的技术复合词；每个词都在同一个抽象名词前加拉丁或希腊修饰语，标出程度、宿主或层级。

note.en: The first group separates the abstract noun from the actor and the adjective. The second group holds other ecological relationships that differ in who pays and who benefits.
note.cn: 第一组区分抽象名词与行动者、形容词；第二组是其他生态关系，区别在于谁付账、谁受益。

entries.definition: The organism that lives at the host's expense. Parasitism names the relationship, parasite names one partner.
entries.definitionCN: 靠宿主供养的生物；parasitism 命名关系，parasite 命名其中一方。

entries.definition: Describing a way of life. It can modify disease, worm or plant, while parasitism is the abstract noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述生活方式的形容词，可修饰疾病、蠕虫或植物；而 parasitism 是抽象名词。

entries.definition: To infest a host as a parasite. It is the action, not the relationship seen as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指以寄生物方式侵染宿主；它是动作，而不是被整体看待的关系。

entries.definition: A relationship in which both partners gain. It is the positive counterpart of parasitism, not a variant of it.
entries.definitionCN: 双方都获益的关系；它是 parasitism 的正面对应，而不是其变体。

entries.definition: A relationship in which one partner gains and the other is neither helped nor harmed. It is milder than parasitism because the host pays no cost.
entries.definitionCN: 一方获益、另一方既不受益也不受损的关系；它比 parasitism 温和，因为宿主不付代价。

entries.definition: The act of using another for one's own advantage. It is the general social meaning that parasitism narrows to a way of life.
entries.definitionCN: 为自身利益利用他者的行为；它是泛指的社会含义，parasitism 则把它收窄为一种生活方式。

entries.definition: A disease caused by parasites. It names the medical condition, while parasitism names the relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 由寄生物引起的疾病；它命名医学状况，而 parasitism 命名关系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: parasite + -ism: the practice, not the practitioner; the relationship, not the organism.
normal.cn: parasite + -ism：指做法，不指从业者；指关系，不指生物。

normal.en: The human sense arrived in the 1610s; the biological sense only by 1840.
normal.cn: 指人的义项在十七世纪十年代出现，生物学义到 1840 年才有。

normal.en: The family runs parasite, parasitic, parasitism, parasitize, parasitology and hyperparasitism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 parasite、parasitic、parasitism、parasitize、parasitology、hyperparasitism。

normal.en: Obligate means the host is required; facultative means the host is optional.
normal.cn: 专性表示宿主是必需的，兼性表示宿主是可选的。

normal.en: Three costs can be transferred: food from a body, care for young, and rent for a life.
normal.cn: 可转移的成本有三种：身体里的食物、对幼崽的照料，以及生活的房租。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow that only points one way, from host to guest.
abstract.cn: 想象一支只朝一个方向的箭头，从宿主指向来客。

abstract.en: Picture a nest where the real mother never returns.
abstract.cn: 想象一个巢，真正的母亲再也不回来。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder of hosts, each carrying the one above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一架宿主叠成的梯子，每一层都背着上面一层。

examples.en: Parasitism can drive the evolution of new defences in hosts.
examples.cn: 寄生关系能推动宿主演化出新的防御。

examples.en: Brood parasitism is common among certain warblers and cowbirds.
examples.cn: 巢寄生在某些莺类与灶巢鸟中很常见。

examples.en: The study measured parasitism across twelve lakes.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了十二个湖泊中的寄生率。

dict_mnemonic.text: parasite（寄生物）+ -ism（……主义、……关系）→ 寄生的关系 → parasitism 寄生

root: 希腊 para-「在旁边」+ sitos「食物」→ parasitos「在别人桌上吃饭的人」→ 英语 parasite（1530s）→ parasite + -ism → parasitism（1610s 社会义；1840 年出现生物学义）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the biological relationship to its social form, its nest form, its two dependence types, its stacked form, its measured rate and its status as an evolutionary strategy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从生物学关系出发，走向它的社会形式、巢中形式、两种依赖类型、叠层形式、可测比率，以及作为演化策略的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two bodies side by side, with a one-way arrow of nutrients between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：并排的两个身体，中间一支单向的养分箭头。

branches.en: RELATIONSHIP: the core abstract sense, one benefits and one is harmed.
branches.cn: 关系：核心抽象义，一方获益、一方受损。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED COST: the cost can be food, rent or parental care, and the host can be a household or a nest.
branches.cn: 转移的成本：成本可以是食物、房租或育雏，宿主可以是家庭或鸟巢。

branches.en: DEGREE: obligate and facultative measure whether the host is a necessity or an option.
branches.cn: 程度：专性与兼性衡量宿主是必需还是可选。

branches.en: LEVEL: hyperparasitism stacks the relationship so that a parasite becomes a host.
branches.cn: 层级：超寄生把关系叠起来，使寄生物反过来成为宿主。

branches.en: MEASURE AND STRATEGY: ecology counts how often it happens, and evolution treats it as a route to survival.
branches.cn: 测量与策略：生态学数它发生的频率，演化论把它当作一条生存路线。

intro.en: Parasitism is a Greek compound noun with a Greek abstract suffix: beside, food, and the name of a practice.
intro.cn: parasitism 是带希腊抽象后缀的希腊复合名词：旁边、食物，以及一种做法的名称。

latinIntro.en: Latin parasitus supplied the base noun, and Latin -ismus supplied the abstract ending. The word is English, but both parts reached it through Latinized forms of Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 parasitus 提供了基础名词，拉丁 -ismus 提供了抽象词尾；这个词是英语词，但两个部分都经希腊语的拉丁化形式传入。

items.exampleCN: 寄生关系塑造了宿主的防御。

items.meaning: one who lives at another's expense
items.example: The parasite left the host alive.
A parasitic insect fed on the bird.
items.exampleCN: 一种寄生昆虫以这只鸟为食。
寄生虫学解释了宿主专一性。

items.meaningCN: 寄生物又被另一种生物寄生
items.exampleCN: 超寄生控制着某些害虫种群。

items.example: Endoparasitism requires tolerance of host defences.
items.exampleCN: 体内寄生需要耐受宿主的防御。

items.meaning: parasitism on the surface of a host
items.exampleCN: 体表寄生在宿主之间易于传播。

items.meaning: laying eggs for another bird to raise
items.example: Brood parasitism saves the female time.
items.exampleCN: 巢寄生为雌鸟节省时间。

definition_zh: 使稳定；使稳固；稳定下来；使（价格、病情）趋于平稳
definition_en: to make something steady or keep it from changing, and also to become steady without outside help
core_image: 拍摄现场，一只手扶住晃动的三脚架，另一只手把最后一个旋钮拧紧，取景框里的画面终于不再抖
scene: 拍摄现场，一只手扶住晃动的三脚架，另一只手把最后一个旋钮拧紧，取景框里的画面终于不再抖。 A heavy base helped stabilize the tower before the storm arrived.
sceneCN: 这里指使实物稳固、不再晃动（第 1 个义项：使物体保持稳定）；句意为在暴风雨到来之前，一个沉重的底座帮助把塔架稳定住。

pos.zh: 使稳定；使稳固；稳定下来；使趋于平稳

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「稳定化；稳定过程」
由该动词加表示施动者或器具的名词尾构成，义为「稳定器；安定剂」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已稳定的」
由该动词的现在分词转成的形容词，义为「起稳定作用的」

senses.title: Make an object steady in place
senses.definition: to fix something physically so that it no longer rocks, shifts or falls
senses.definitionCN: 从物理上固定某物，使它不再摇晃、移动或倒下
senses.example: Steel props were used to stabilize the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 人们用钢支撑把那段墙稳住。
senses.why: The word is built on an adjective meaning able to stand, so the first job it does is keep a thing standing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在「能够站立」的形容词之上，所以它的第一件工作就是让东西立住。

senses.title: Keep a quantity at a fixed level
senses.definition: to hold temperature, pressure or another measurable quantity near one value
senses.definitionCN: 把温度、压力或其他可测量的量维持在某一数值附近
senses.example: A thermostat helps stabilize the temperature inside the room.
senses.exampleCN: 恒温器有助于把室内温度保持稳定。
senses.why: A quantity that does not drift is steady in the same sense as a table that does not wobble.
senses.whyCN: 一个不漂移的数值，和一张不晃的桌子，是同一个意义上的「稳」。

senses.title: Calm a situation or relationship
senses.definition: to keep a conflict, market mood or negotiation from breaking apart
senses.definitionCN: 使冲突、市场情绪或谈判不至于崩散
senses.example: The mediator tried to stabilize the talks after the quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后，调解人试图让谈判重新稳定下来。
senses.why: Human affairs also wobble, and the same word is used for the hand that keeps them from tipping over.
senses.whyCN: 人间事务也会摇晃，同一个词也用来形容那只不让局面倾覆的手。

senses.title: Steady a patient's condition
senses.definition: in medicine, to bring vital signs under control so that the patient is no longer in immediate danger
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指把生命体征控制住，使病人脱离即刻危险
senses.example: Doctors worked all night to stabilize the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们整夜工作，使病人的情况稳定下来。
senses.why: A body in crisis is described as unstable, so the verb naturally names the work of bringing it back to a steady state.
senses.whyCN: 危急中的身体被称为「不稳定」，于是这个动词自然用来指把它带回稳定状态的工作。

senses.title: Become steady by itself
senses.definition: of a thing or condition that settles without anyone acting on it
senses.definitionCN: 指事物或状况无需他人作用便自行安定
senses.example: The plane's altitude began to stabilize after the turbulence.
senses.exampleCN: 颠簸之后，飞机的高度开始稳定下来。
senses.why: This is the intransitive use, where the subject is the thing that settles rather than the hand that settles it.
senses.whyCN: 这是不及物用法，主语是安定下来的事物，而不是使它安定的那只手。

senses.title: Keep a chemical substance from changing
senses.definition: to prevent a compound, mixture or material from decomposing or reacting further
senses.definitionCN: 防止化合物、混合物或材料分解或继续反应
senses.example: A little acid was added to stabilize the solution.
senses.exampleCN: 加入少量酸以使溶液保持稳定。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the everyday word because a substance that does not break down is steady in the most literal way.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了这个日常词，因为不分解的物质正是最字面意义上的「稳」。

senses.title: Hold a currency or market firm
senses.definition: of a government or bank, to stop a currency or market from swinging sharply
senses.definitionCN: 指政府或银行阻止货币或市场剧烈波动
senses.example: The central bank moved to stabilize the currency.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行采取行动稳住货币。
senses.why: Money is measured like temperature, and a rate that stops swinging is called stable in every financial report.
senses.whyCN: 货币像温度一样被计量，而止住摆动的汇率在每份金融报告里都被称为稳定。

senses.title: Restore the balance of a craft
senses.titleCN: 使飞行器或船只恢复平衡
senses.definition: of a pilot or helmsman, to bring an aircraft or vessel back to level flight or an even keel
senses.definitionCN: 指飞行员或舵手使飞行器或船只恢复水平飞行或平稳航行
senses.example: The pilot had to stabilize the aircraft in the crosswind.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员必须在侧风中把飞机稳住。
senses.why: A craft out of balance is unstable, and the verb describes the correction that returns it to level.
senses.whyCN: 失去平衡的飞行器是不稳定的，而这个动词描述的正是把它带回水平的那一修正。

senses.title: Bring a natural system toward balance
senses.definition: of an ecosystem or climate, to reduce swings so that the system stays within a workable range
senses.definitionCN: 指生态系统或气候，减少波动使系统停留在可运转的范围内
senses.example: Wetland restoration can help stabilize the local climate.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地修复有助于使当地气候趋于稳定。
senses.why: The largest systems are described with the smallest image: a hand steadying something that would otherwise sway.
senses.whyCN: 最大的系统用最小的意象来描述：一只手稳住本来会摇摆的东西。

intro.en: Stabilize is an English verb formed from stable plus the verb ending -ize. Stable came through French from Latin stabilis, able to stand, which rests on stare, to stand.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语在 stable 之上加动词词尾构成的，而 stable 经法语来自拉丁语 stabilis「能够站立的」，其底层是 stare「站立」。

items.en: Stare meant to stand or remain in place, and it is the ground under a large family of standing words.
items.cn: stare 意为站立或留在原处，是一大批表示「站立」的词的根基。

items.en: The adjective meant firm or able to stand, used of posts, positions and later of character.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为牢固的、能站住的，先用于柱子与位置，后来也用于性格。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective to English, where it named buildings for animals before it named anything else.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词带进英语，它在那里最先指关牲口的棚舍。

items.en: The English adjective added the sense of enduring and free from sudden change.
items.cn: 英语中的形容词义增加了「持久、不易突变」的意思。

items.en: The verb appeared in the nineteenth century, first in technical writing about ships and machines; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十九世纪出现，最早见于关于船只与机器的技术写作；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Medicine, finance and climate science each took the verb and gave it a specialised object.
items.cn: 医学、金融与气候科学各自取用这个动词，并给它配上专门的对象。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like stabilize; the second group names neighbouring ideas of steadiness.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 stabilize 相近；第二组是与「稳、安定」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Firm and not likely to move or change; the adjective behind the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指牢固、不易移动或改变的，是本词背后的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being steady and unlikely to change.
entries.definitionCN: 指稳定、不易改变的状态。

entries.definition: A device or substance that keeps something steady.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物保持稳定的装置或物质。

entries.definition: The act of making something steady or keeping it at a level.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物稳定或使其保持在一定水平的行为。

entries.definition: Not steady and likely to change or fall; it negates the adjective rather than deriving from the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指不稳定、容易变化或倒塌的；它否定的是形容词，而不是从动词派生。

entries.definition: To make something stop shaking, often by holding it; it stresses the motion that stops.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物不再晃动，常含用手扶住之意；它强调停止的那个动作。

entries.definition: To keep something from falling to one side, stressing equal weight rather than freedom from change.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物不向一侧倾倒，强调重量均衡而非不变。

entries.definition: To fasten something so that it cannot be moved or taken, stressing attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物固定住使其无法移动或被拿走，强调固定连接。

entries.definition: To come to rest after movement, often without outside help; close to the intransitive sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指运动之后静止下来，常无需外力；接近本词的不及物义项。

entries.definition: To make something solid or fixed, stressing resistance to pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物坚实或固定，强调抗压能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the standing root, the adjective behind the verb and the many fields that borrowed it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「站立」的词根、动词背后的形容词，以及借用过它的众多领域。

normal.en: The root means to stand, so to stabilize is to help something keep standing.
normal.cn: 词根意为站立，所以「使稳定」就是帮某物一直站住。

normal.en: A table with one short leg wobbles; a folded paper under that leg stabilizes it.
normal.cn: 桌子有一条短腿就会晃，在腿下垫一张折好的纸就把它稳住了。

normal.en: A stabilizer bar on a car does the same job as the outrigger on a boat.
normal.cn: 汽车上的稳定杆，和船上的舷外浮架做的是同一件事。

normal.en: Doctors say a patient is stable when the numbers stop swinging, which is the medical face of the word.
normal.cn: 医生说病人情况稳定，是指各项数值不再大幅摆动，这就是这个词的医学面孔。

normal.en: The word is transitive or intransitive: a hand stabilizes a ladder, and a ladder stabilizes by itself.
normal.cn: 这个词既可及物也可不及物：一只手稳住梯子，梯子也会自行稳定下来。

abstract.en: To stabilize is not to freeze; it is to keep change small enough to live with.
abstract.cn: 使稳定并不是使冻结，而是把变化控制到可以共处的程度。

abstract.en: Every stabilizing act chooses which movements matter and which can be ignored.
abstract.cn: 每一次稳定动作都在选择哪些晃动要紧、哪些可以不管。

abstract.en: A system is called stable when it can absorb a push and still return to its shape.
abstract.cn: 一个系统被称为稳定，是因为它能吸收一次推挤之后仍回到原来的形状。

examples.en: The crew used ropes to stabilize the mast in the wind.
examples.cn: 船员用绳索在风中把桅杆稳住。

examples.en: The government cut spending to stabilize the currency.
examples.cn: 政府削减开支以稳住货币。

examples.en: Her pulse began to stabilize after the second dose.
examples.cn: 第二剂药之后，她的脉搏开始稳定下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「斯泰波赖兹」——「斯泰」像「死抬」，四个人死抬一张桌子，桌子就稳了：使稳定

root: 拉丁语 stare「站立」→ stabilis「能站立的、牢固的」→ 法语 estable → 英语 stable「稳定的」→ 加动词词尾构成 stabilize「使稳定」；词义由「站住」扩展为「数值、病情、市场不摆动」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from a hand holding an object to a body, a market and a whole climate: physical support, fixed levels, calm relations, medical control, self-settling, chemical stability, currency, craft balance and natural systems.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一只手扶住物体，走向身体、市场与整个气候：物理支撑、数值恒定、关系缓和、病情控制、自行安定、化学稳定、货币、航行平衡与自然系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tightening the last knob on a shaking tripod until the frame stops moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拧紧晃动三脚架上的最后一个旋钮，直到画面不再移动。

branches.en: THE SUPPORT BRANCH: props hold a wall, and a pilot brings an aircraft back to level.
branches.cn: 支撑分支：支柱撑住墙，飞行员把飞行器带回水平。

branches.en: THE LEVEL BRANCH: a thermostat holds temperature and a central bank holds a currency.
branches.cn: 水平分支：恒温器稳住温度，中央银行稳住货币。

branches.en: THE RELATIONS BRANCH: a mediator keeps talks from tipping over.
branches.cn: 关系分支：调解人使谈判不至于倾覆。

branches.en: THE BODY BRANCH: doctors steady a patient, and a pulse settles on its own.
branches.cn: 身体分支：医生稳住病人，脉搏也会自行安定。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL AND SYSTEM BRANCH: acid keeps a solution from breaking down, and wetlands keep a climate within range.
branches.cn: 材料与系统分支：酸使溶液不分解，湿地使气候停留在可运转的范围内。

intro.en: Stabilize is an English verb built on a Latin adjective of standing, with a productive verb ending doing the work of making.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立于拉丁语「站立」形容词之上的英语动词，由能产的动词词尾承担「使成为」的工作。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb of standing, its adjective and a later verb of making firm; English adds its own verb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供表示站立的动词、其形容词以及后来表示「使牢固」的动词；英语加上自己的动词词尾。

items.structure: English verb-forming suffix through French and Latin
items.example: It turns the adjective into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表示「使成为」的动词。

items.example: The adjective supplies the meaning the verb carries.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供动词所承载的意义。

items.example: The Latin adjective already implies resistance to falling.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词已经含有「抗倒塌」的意思。

items.example: Standing is the physical picture under all the senses.
items.exampleCN: 站立是所有义项底下的物理图像。

items.example: It forms the noun for the process of making steady.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「使稳定」这一过程的名词。

items.meaning: one that does or a device that does
items.meaningCN: 做某事者；起某作用的器具
items.example: It names the device that keeps a thing steady.
items.exampleCN: 它命名使某物保持稳定的装置。

items.example: It forms the noun for the quality of standing firm.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「稳固」性质的名词。

items.meaning: action or result of making or becoming
items.meaningCN: 使……或变为……的行为或结果
items.example: It forms stabilization, the act of making steady.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 stabilization，即「使稳定的行为」。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「稳定化；稳定过程」
由该动词加表示施动者或器具的名词尾构成，义为「稳定器；安定剂」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已稳定的」
由该动词的现在分词转成的形容词，义为「起稳定作用的」

definition_zh: 正态分布；高斯分布；钟形分布；标准正态分布
definition_en: a continuous probability distribution whose values cluster symmetrically around a mean, forming a bell-shaped curve
core_image: 一座左右对称的钟形山丘，正中最高，向两侧缓缓落平
scene: 测量数据大多聚在中间，越往两端越少，形成一条对称的曲线。 Most measurements in the sample follow a normal distribution.
sceneCN: 这里指「数值围绕平均值对称聚集、两端渐稀的那种分布」（第 1 个义项：正态分布）；句意为样本中的大多数测量值服从正态分布。可辨识物件：坐标轴、对称曲线、中心线、刻度。

pos.zh: 正态分布；高斯分布；钟形分布

senses.title: The symmetric probability distribution
senses.definition: a continuous distribution in which values cluster symmetrically about a mean
senses.definitionCN: 数值围绕平均值对称聚集的连续分布
senses.example: Most measurements in the sample follow a normal distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 样本中大多数测量值服从正态分布。
senses.why: The curve rises to a single peak at the mean and falls away equally on both sides, which is why the name speaks of a rule or pattern.
senses.whyCN: 曲线在平均值处升到唯一的峰，两侧对称下落，因此这个名称说的是某种「规矩」或「范式」。

senses.title: The bell-shaped curve
senses.definition: the graph of such a distribution, shaped like a bell
senses.definitionCN: 这种分布的图形，形状像一口钟
senses.example: The data were plotted as a smooth bell curve.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数据被画成一条平滑的钟形曲线。
senses.why: Plotting the distribution produces a curve whose outline is easy to recognise, so the picture often replaces the definition.
senses.whyCN: 画出分布就得到一条轮廓易认的曲线，于是图形常代替定义。

senses.title: The standard normal distribution
senses.definition: the special case with a mean of zero and a standard deviation of one
senses.definitionCN: 平均值为零、标准差为一的特例
senses.example: Tables of the standard normal distribution give areas under the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 标准正态分布表给出曲线下的面积。
senses.why: Setting the centre to zero and the spread to one makes every such curve comparable, so one table serves all cases.
senses.whyCN: 把中心定为零、离散定为一，就能让所有这类曲线可比，于是一张表可通用于全部情形。

senses.title: The Gaussian distribution
senses.definition: the same distribution under the name of Gauss, who studied its errors
senses.definitionCN: 同一分布以高斯之名称呼，他研究过其中的误差
senses.example: The Gaussian distribution appears in his work on astronomical errors.
senses.exampleCN: 高斯分布出现在他关于天文误差的研究中。
senses.why: A second name honours an early user rather than describing the shape; both names refer to one object.
senses.whyCN: 另一个名称纪念一位早期使用者，而不是描述形状；两个名称指同一个对象。

senses.title: The model for measurement errors
senses.definition: the assumed distribution of random errors around a true value
senses.definitionCN: 随机误差围绕真值分布的假设模型
senses.example: Repeated readings spread in a normal distribution around the true weight.
senses.exampleCN: 重复读数围绕真实重量呈正态分布散开。
senses.why: Errors small and large cancel in a way that produces a symmetric curve, which is why measurement adopted this model.
senses.whyCN: 大大小小的误差以一种方式相互抵消，产生对称曲线，测量学因此采用这个模型。

senses.title: The limiting distribution in the central limit theorem
senses.titleCN: 中心极限定理中的极限分布
senses.definition: the distribution that sums of many independent values approach
senses.definitionCN: 许多独立数值之和所趋近的分布
senses.example: Sums of many independent shocks approach a normal distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 许多独立冲击之和趋近正态分布。
senses.why: Adding many independent contributions smooths away their individual shapes, leaving the same symmetric curve, which explains how widely it appears.
senses.whyCN: 把许多独立贡献相加会抹平各自的形状，只剩同一条对称曲线，这解释了它为何到处出现。

senses.title: The object of normality tests
senses.definition: the pattern that data are compared with in a test of normality
senses.definitionCN: 正态性检验中用来与数据比较的那种模式
senses.example: The normality test asked whether the residuals were close enough to a normal distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 正态性检验问的是：残差是否足够接近正态分布。
senses.why: Because methods often assume the distribution, checking whether data resemble it became a standard step.
senses.whyCN: 由于方法常以此分布为前提，检查数据是否像它就成了标准步骤。

senses.title: The abstract shape of clustering at the centre
senses.titleCN: 抽象：居中密集、两端稀少的形态
senses.definition: any pattern in which most things sit near the middle and few at the edges
senses.definitionCN: 任何多数靠中间、少数在边缘的形态
senses.example: Awards in that field follow a normal distribution, with most near the middle.
senses.exampleCN: 那个领域的奖项呈正态分布，多数落在中间。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps only the silhouette, applying the bell to anything that thins out at both ends.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留轮廓，把这口钟用在任何两端渐稀的事物上。

intro.en: Normal distribution joins Latin norma 'a carpenter's square, a rule' and Latin distribuere 'to allot'. The mathematical phrase took shape in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: normal distribution 由拉丁 norma「木匠的曲尺、规矩」与拉丁 distribuere「分配」合成；这个数学短语在十九世纪成形。

items.en: Norma meant a carpenter's square, and so a rule or a pattern. Its further origin is uncertain, and any older root suggested for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: norma 指木匠的曲尺，因此也指规矩、范式。其更早来源不确定，凡为其拟出的更古老词根都属假说。

items.en: Normalis meant 'made according to a square', hence right-angled and then regular, conforming to a rule.
items.cn: normalis 意为「按曲尺做成的」，因此指直角，再引申为合规矩、合乎范式。

items.en: Tribuere 'to allot, assign' is generally connected with tribus 'tribe', from the practice of assigning by tribe; the origin of tribus itself is not settled.
items.cn: tribuere「分配、分派」一般认为与 tribus「部族」有关，源于按部族分派的做法；tribus 本身的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus tribuere gave distribuere 'to divide up, distribute', and distributio named the division.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加 tribuere 构成 distribuere「分给、分配」，名词 distributio 指这种分配。

items.en: The phrase normal distribution emerged in the nineteenth century as error theory and statistics converged; Gauss studied the error curve, and the adjective normal became standard in the 1890s.
items.cn: 这个短语在十九世纪随误差理论与统计学的汇合而出现；高斯研究过误差曲线，而形容词「正常的」在十九世纪九十年代成为标准叫法。

items.en: Gaussian distribution and bell curve are alternative names with their own histories; exact first citations for the English phrase vary, so dates here are approximate.
items.cn: 高斯分布与钟形曲线是各有来历的别名；这个英语短语的确切首见书证各有出入，此处年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds names and near-relatives of the same distribution; group two holds other distributions and words for spread.
note.cn: 第一组是同一分布的名称与近亲；第二组是其他分布以及表示离散的词。

entries.definition: An older and more descriptive name for the graph of the distribution, stressing the outline rather than the probability law.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧也更具描述性的名称，指这条曲线本身，强调轮廓而非概率规律。

entries.definition: The case with mean zero and standard deviation one, used to compare all others.
entries.definitionCN: 平均值为零、标准差为一的特例，用来比较其他所有情形。

entries.definition: The distribution of a variable whose logarithm is normal; it is skewed, not symmetric.
entries.definitionCN: 某个变量的对数服从正态分布时该变量的分布；它是偏斜的，并不对称。

entries.definition: The use of the normal curve to approximate another distribution, as with large samples.
entries.definitionCN: 用正态曲线近似另一种分布的方法，如大样本情形。

entries.definition: The same object named after Gauss, common in physics and engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 同一对象以高斯命名，常见于物理与工程。

entries.definition: The everyday name for the shape, often used outside technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 这种形状的日常叫法，常用于技术写作之外。

entries.definition: The distribution of the number of successes in fixed trials, discrete rather than continuous.
entries.definitionCN: 固定次数试验中成功次数的分布，是离散的而非连续的。

entries.definition: The distribution of counts of rare events in a fixed interval.
entries.definitionCN: 固定区间内稀有事件计数的分布。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first word means 'according to a rule', the second means 'a dividing up': a regular way of spreading values.
normal.cn: 前一个词意为「合乎规矩」，后一个词意为「分配」：一种有规律的数值铺开方式。

normal.en: One family runs normal, normality, normalize, normally distributed and distribution.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：正常的、正态性、使标准化、呈正态分布的、分布。

normal.en: Two names point at one object: the descriptive bell curve and the honorific Gaussian distribution.
normal.cn: 两个名称指同一个对象：描述形状的钟形曲线，与纪念高斯的正态分布。

normal.en: The special case with centre zero and spread one is the standard normal, the one tables are printed for.
normal.cn: 中心为零、离散为一的特例是标准正态，表格就是为它印的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: follow a normal distribution, assume a normal distribution, test for normality.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：服从正态分布、假定服从正态分布、做正态性检验。

abstract.en: Picture a hill symmetric on both sides, steepest halfway down and flattening at the edges.
abstract.cn: 想象一座左右对称的山丘，半腰最陡，边缘渐渐变平。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd standing around a fountain, dense at the centre and thinning toward the walls.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人围在喷泉边，中间密，靠墙处渐稀。

abstract.en: Picture a target where most shots fall near the bullseye and only a few reach the outer ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一个靶子，多数弹着点落在靶心附近，只有少数到了外环。

examples.en: The residuals were close to a normal distribution.
examples.cn: 残差接近正态分布。

examples.en: Heights in the sample are normally distributed.
examples.cn: 样本中的身高呈正态分布。

examples.en: To use the table, convert the values to the standard normal distribution.
examples.cn: 要用这张表，先把数值换算成标准正态分布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 前一个词意为「合乎规矩」，后一个词意为「分配」：数值按一种有规律的样式铺开，中间密、两端稀，画出来就是一口钟。

root: 复合术语。normal 出自拉丁 normalis「按曲尺做成的」，词根 norma 指木匠曲尺，更早来源不确定；distribution 出自拉丁 distribuere「分配」＝ dis-（分开）＋ tribuere「分派」，tribuere 一般认为与 tribus「部族」有关。这个短语在十九世纪成形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one silhouette: values pile up at the centre and thin out at both ends. The silhouette is then given a probability law, a curve, a standard case, a second name, an error model, a limiting law, a test and, at last, a plain shape for anything that behaves that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述同一个轮廓：数值在中间堆高，两端渐稀。这个轮廓再依次获得概率规律、曲线、标准特例、第二个名称、误差模型、极限规律、一种检验，最后成为任何如此表现之物的朴素形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a symmetric hill, highest at the centre and flattening toward both edges.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座左右对称的山丘，正中最高，向两侧渐渐变平。

branches.en: THE SHAPE AND THE LAW: the probability rule and the curve drawn from it are one object seen twice.
branches.cn: 形状与规律：概率规则与由它画出的曲线，是同一对象的两种看法。

branches.en: THE SPECIAL CASE: centre zero and spread one make every curve comparable.
branches.cn: 标准特例：中心为零、离散为一，使所有曲线可比。

branches.en: TWO NAMES: an honorific name and a descriptive name point at the same distribution.
branches.cn: 两个名称：纪念性名称与描述性名称指向同一个分布。

branches.en: WHY IT APPEARS: error theory and the summing of independent values both produce this curve.
branches.cn: 为何出现：误差理论与独立数值求和都产生这条曲线。

branches.en: THE TEST AND THE SHAPE: data are checked against it, and any centre-heavy pattern is called by its outline.
branches.cn: 检验与形状：数据要对照它来检查，而任何中间密集的形态都以它的轮廓命名。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin word for a rule and a Latin verb for allotting, so each half can be read with its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表示「规矩」的拉丁词与一个表示「分派」的拉丁动词接在一起，两半各自可连同词族来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma gives normal and normalis; Latin tribuere gives distribute, contribution and tribute.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 norma 给出 normal 与 normalis；拉丁 tribuere 给出 distribute、contribution、tribute。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of a standard pattern.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「标准范式」的意思。

items.meaning: made according to a square; regular
items.meaningCN: 按曲尺做成的；合规矩的
items.example: The adjective turns the rule into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把规矩变成一种性质。

items.example: The root supplies the act of handing out.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「分发出去」的动作。

items.example: The verb spreads values across a range.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把数值铺到一个范围里。

items.meaning: the act or result of spreading out
to give out over a range
items.example: The values distribute around the centre.

definition_zh: 稳定；稳定性；稳固；安定；（化学）稳定性
definition_en: the quality of remaining firm, steady and unlikely to change or collapse
core_image: 一座宽基座的高塔在风中仍然直立，塔尖几乎不动
scene: 这里指「稳定」。 The bridge's stability was tested by loading it with trucks far heavier than expected.
sceneCN: 这里 stability 指「结构稳定性」（第 1 个义项：在外力下保持不倒的能力）；桥被远超预期的卡车载重检验。图中可辨识物件：桥梁、成排卡车、位移标尺、支座。

pos.zh: 稳定；稳定性；稳固；安定；化学稳定性（多不可数，指多种稳定性质时用复数 stabilities）

senses.title: Firmness of structure
senses.titleCN: 结构稳固：外力下不倾覆
senses.definition: the ability of a structure to stay upright and resist collapse
senses.definitionCN: 结构保持直立、抵抗坍塌的能力
senses.example: The tower's stability comes from its wide base.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔的稳固来自它宽阔的基座。
senses.why: Latin stabilitas meant 'firmness', from stabilis 'standing firm', built on stare 'to stand'; the noun names the capacity to keep standing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 stabilitas 意为「坚固」，出自 stabilis「站得稳的」，而后者基于 stare「站立」；这个名词命名的是「保持站住」的能力。

senses.title: Steadiness of character
senses.titleCN: 性情稳定：情绪不起大落
senses.definition: emotional steadiness, the quality of not being easily thrown off
senses.definitionCN: 情绪上的平稳，不易被扰动
senses.example: Her stability helped the team through the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 她的沉稳帮助团队度过了危机。
senses.why: The standing image moves inward: a person who stands firm is emotionally stable.
senses.whyCN: 站立的意象向内移动：站得稳的人，在情绪上就是稳定的。

senses.title: Economic stability
senses.titleCN: 经济稳定：价格与产出少波动
senses.definition: in economics, the condition in which prices and output change slowly and predictably
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中价格与产出变化缓慢而可预期的状态
senses.example: Central banks aim at price stability rather than zero inflation.
senses.exampleCN: 央行追求价格稳定，而非零通胀。
senses.why: Economics borrows 'standing firm' for a system: stability is the absence of sharp swings.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借「站得稳」来描述系统：稳定就是没有剧烈摆动。

senses.title: Political stability
senses.titleCN: 政治稳定：秩序持续不被打破
senses.definition: the condition in which a government and its institutions endure without upheaval
senses.definitionCN: 政府及其制度持续存续、不发生剧变的状态
senses.example: Foreign investment depends on political stability.
senses.exampleCN: 外国投资取决于政治稳定。
senses.why: The word widened from objects to institutions: what stands firm can also be a state.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从物体拓宽到制度：站得稳的也可以是一个国家。

senses.title: Mechanical equilibrium
senses.titleCN: 力学平衡：受扰后能回到原位
senses.definition: in physics, the tendency of a system to return to equilibrium after a small disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 物理中系统受到小扰动后回到平衡的趋势
senses.example: The ball at the bottom of the bowl has stability; at the top it does not.
senses.exampleCN: 碗底的球是稳定的，碗顶的球则不稳定。
senses.why: Physics made the notion testable: stability is defined by what happens after a nudge.
senses.whyCN: 物理学让这一概念可被检验：稳定性由「被轻推之后会怎样」来定义。

senses.title: Chemical stability
senses.titleCN: 化学稳定性：不易分解或反应
senses.definition: in chemistry, the resistance of a substance to decomposition or unwanted reaction
senses.definitionCN: 化学中物质抵抗分解或非期望反应的能力
senses.example: The compound's thermal stability limits its use at high temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 该化合物的热稳定性限制了它在高温下的使用。
senses.why: Chemists measure how long a substance holds together, which is the standing image at molecular scale.
senses.whyCN: 化学家测量物质能保持完整多久，这就是分子尺度上的「站住」意象。

senses.title: Ecological stability
senses.titleCN: 生态稳定：扰动后仍能维持结构
senses.definition: in ecology, the capacity of an ecosystem to maintain its structure after disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统中受扰动后维持其结构的能力
senses.example: Species diversity contributes to the stability of the grassland.
senses.exampleCN: 物种多样性有助于草地的稳定。
senses.why: Ecology applies the same test: a system is stable if it returns after a shock, not if it never changes.
senses.whyCN: 生态学应用同样的检验：系统若在冲击后恢复才算稳定，而非从不变化。

senses.title: Medical stability
senses.titleCN: 病情稳定：指标不再恶化
senses.definition: in medicine, the condition of a patient whose vital signs are not worsening
senses.definitionCN: 医学中病人生命体征不再恶化的状态
senses.example: The patient is now in stable condition and can be moved.
senses.exampleCN: 病人现在病情稳定，可以转运。
senses.why: Clinical usage compresses the idea into a status word: stable means no longer moving in the wrong direction.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法把这一观念压缩为状态词：stable 意为不再朝错误方向变化。

intro.en: Stability comes from Latin stabilitas 'firmness', from stabilis 'standing firm', built on stare 'to stand'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: stability 出自拉丁 stabilitas「坚固」，源自 stabilis「站得稳的」，基于 stare「站立」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin stare meant 'to stand, to remain'. It is well recorded and underlies state, status, station, statue and constant; its deeper origin is debated.
items.cn: 拉丁 stare 意为「站立、停留」。记录充分，支撑 state、status、station、statue、constant；其更深来源有争议。

items.en: Stabilis 'standing firm, steadfast' described what does not give way. The adjective served both physical and moral firmness.
items.cn: stabilis「站得稳的、坚定的」描述不屈服的东西。这个形容词既用于物理的稳固，也用于道德上的坚定。

items.en: The noun stabilitas named firmness as a quality. It is classical, used of buildings, of character and of political order.
items.cn: 名词 stabilitas 命名作为性质的坚固。它属古典用法，可用于建筑、性格与政治秩序。

items.en: English stability arrives through French in the Middle Ages, first in the sense of firmness of mind or of realm. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 stability 经法语于中世纪进入，初义为心志或国度的稳固。最早确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word entered mechanics and chemistry, where stability became a measurable response to disturbance.
items.cn: 自 17 世纪起，这个词进入力学与化学，稳定性在那里成为对扰动的可测响应。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation date only): the first English date is uncertain; the origin of stare before its 'stand' sense is debated and any Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：英语首见年代存疑；stare 在「站立」义之前的来源有争议，任何印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: The first group holds same-family words that differ in part of speech; the second holds near-synonyms for steadiness.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词，区别在词性；第二组是表示平稳的近义词。

entries.definition: As an adjective it means 'firm'; as a noun it means a building for horses. Stability is only the abstract noun.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词意为「稳固的」；作名词指马厩。stability 只是抽象名词。

entries.definition: To make something steady. It names the action; stability is the state achieved.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物稳定。它命名动作；stability 是达到的状态。

entries.definition: The lack of stability, often suggesting tendency to change suddenly. It is not the same as mere change.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏稳定，常暗示易于突变。它与单纯的「变化」并不相同。

entries.definition: The process of making something stable, as in economic stabilization. Stability is the resulting condition.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变稳的过程，如经济稳定化。stability 是结果状态。

entries.definition: Freedom from shaking or sudden change. It stresses evenness, while stability stresses resistance to being moved.
entries.definitionCN: 不摇晃、不突变。它强调均匀，而 stability 强调抵抗被推动。

entries.definition: Solidity of material or of purpose. It is more physical and more about texture than stability.
entries.definitionCN: 材料或意志的坚实。它更偏物理，更关乎质地。

entries.definition: A state in which opposing forces balance. It can be unstable equilibrium, so it does not guarantee stability.
entries.definitionCN: 对立力量相互平衡的状态。它可以是「不稳定平衡」，因此并不保证稳定。

entries.definition: The quality of staying the same. It stresses lack of change, while stability allows change that returns to a level.
entries.definitionCN: 保持不变的性质。它强调不变，而 stability 允许回到某一水平的变化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: stare 'to stand' + -bilis 'able' + -itas: the ability to keep standing.
normal.cn: stare「站立」+ -bilis「能够」+ -itas：保持站住的能力。

normal.en: The family runs stable, stability, stabilize, stabilization, stabilizer, instability, establish.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 stable、stability、stabilize、stabilization、stabilizer、instability、establish。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: political stability, price stability, structural stability, thermal stability.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：政治稳定、价格稳定、结构稳定性、热稳定性。

normal.en: The family shares the stare root with state, status, station, statue and constant.
normal.cn: 这个词族与 state、status、station、statue、constant 共享 stare 词根。

normal.en: In physics, stability is tested by a nudge, not by stillness.
normal.cn: 在物理学中，稳定性靠一次轻推来检验，而不是靠静止不动。

abstract.cn: 想象一座高塔，基座比塔顶更宽。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl with a ball resting at the bottom, returning after every push.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗，球停在碗底，每次被推都会回来。

abstract.en: Picture a table with four legs on uneven ground, still not rocking.
abstract.cn: 想象一张四条腿的桌子放在不平的地上，却并不摇晃。

examples.en: Engineers added cross-bracing to improve the stability of the frame.
examples.cn: 工程师增加了交叉支撑，以提高框架的稳定性。

examples.en: Price stability encouraged firms to invest in new equipment.
examples.cn: 价格稳定鼓励企业投资新设备。

examples.en: The patient's condition reached stability after two days in intensive care.
examples.cn: 在重症监护两天后，病人的病情趋于稳定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one upright posture: something keeps standing when pushed, and that capacity can belong to a tower, a temper, a currency, a government, an ecosystem or a patient.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种直立姿态展开：某物在被推动时仍能站住，而这种能力可以属于塔、脾气、货币、政府、生态系统或病人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall tower on a wide base that does not lean in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座宽基座的高塔，在风中并不倾斜。

branches.en: PHYSICAL STANDING: structures and mechanical systems stay up or return after a nudge.
branches.cn: 物理站立：结构与力学系统不倒，或在被推后回到原位。

branches.en: CHARACTER: the same upright image applied to a person's temper.
branches.cn: 性格：同一幅直立意象用于人的性情。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: prices and governments are stable when they do not swing violently.
branches.cn: 系统：价格与政府在不剧烈摆动时就是稳定的。

branches.en: MATTER AND LIFE: compounds resist decomposition, ecosystems recover after shock.
branches.cn: 物质与生命：化合物抵抗分解，生态系统在冲击后恢复。

branches.en: CLINICAL STATUS: a patient stops moving in the wrong direction.
branches.cn: 临床状态：病人不再朝恶化方向变化。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare 'to stand' gives stabilis 'able to stand', and -itas turns it into the abstract noun stabilitas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stare「站立」产生 stabilis「能站住的」，-itas 再把它转为抽象名词 stabilitas。
